Title: Matrix crystallinity and nanofiller compatibility optimization of polyarylether nitrile nanocomposite films for enhanced high-temperature energy storage
Abstract: The rising demand for reliable dielectric materials capable of withstanding prolonged high-temperature operation in next-generation power electronics necessitates innovative material solutions. This study reports a groundbreaking dielectric nanocomposite developed through the in-situ polymerization of polyimide (PI) on barium titanate nanoparticles, forming core–shell structured barium titanate@polyimide (BT@PI) nanohybrids. This approach enhances the nanoparticle-matrix compatibility within the polyarylether nitrile (PEN) composite and modulates the polymer's aggregation morphology. Non-isothermal crystallization analysis revealed a morphological transition from two-dimensional to three-dimensional crystal growth mechanisms upon filler incorporation, with the activation energy rising to 162.51 kJ/mol. Via a comprehensive optimization strategy encompassing interface engineering, crystal structure regulation, and performance integration, these nanocomposites achieve enhanced energy storage characteristics. At ambient temperature, the composite with a low loading of 1 vol% BT@PI exhibits a 73.53 % increase in energy storage density compared to pristine PEN, while maintaining a charge-discharge efficiency exceeding 90 %. Remarkably, even at 150 °C, benefiting from the improved aggregation state structure of the polymer composite, it demonstrates an impressive energy storage density of 2.25 J/cm3 with efficiency remaining above 85 %, while simultaneously delivering a remarkably high charge density of 2.59 J/cm3. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of combining interface engineering and crystallization control strategies, thereby establishing the potential of this composite for high-temperature dielectric applications in advanced power electronic systems. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Effects of different organic macromolecules on the heteroaggregation behavior between nanoplastics and goethite
Abstract: The environmental fate of nanoplastics (NPs) is largely influenced by their heteroaggregation with mineral colloids, a process that is further complicated by the widespread presence of organic macromolecules (OMs) in aqueous systems. This study investigated the differential regulatory mechanisms of four representative types of OMs (humic acid (HA), fulvic acid (FA), sodium alginate (SA), and bovine serum albumin (BSA)) on polystyrene nanoplastics (PSNPs)-goethite heteroaggregation. It was shown that OMs significantly inhibited the heteroaggregation of PSNPs with goethite. This inhibition was attributed to the increased electrostatic repulsion, the introduction of greater physical obstruction, as well as competition over available sites for surface attachment. The inhibiting effect followed the order SA > HA > FA > BSA, which was associated with macromolecular properties and charge density characteristics. Notably, while HA/FA-mediated interactions aligned with classical Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek (DLVO) predictions, SA/BSA systems deviated from DLVO theory calculations, indicating that additional interactions also contributed to the heteroaggregation. The 3D-EEMs and FTIR-2D-COS analyses elucidated the key functional groups and the sequential interactions of various OMs within the PSNP-goethite heteroaggregation process. Overall, the findings advanced mechanistic understanding of NPs-mineral-OMs ternary interactions, providing valuable insights into NPs transport mechanisms and environmental fate in complex aqueous environment. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Enhancement mechanism of electrokinetic remediation of a Cu- and Pb-contaminated loess by constructing a multi-electrode configuration
Abstract: The strong adsorption capacity of loess plays a dominant role in limiting the electrokinetic (EK) remediation process. Modified electrokinetic remediation technologies are increasingly being considered for heavy metal contaminated loess, such as the combined use of graphene oxide-alginate composite hydrogel (GOCH) electrode and EK remediation. However, a comprehensive understanding of the complex interplay of multi-physical fields in the modified EK system with GOCH electrodes remains lacking. Therefore, advanced knowledge in multi-physical field coupling in Cu- and Pb-contaminated loess will be crucial to the practical application of these techniques. This study aimed to validate a two-dimensional numerical model by reproducing the physical properties, electrochemical properties, and adsorption properties of the GOCH electrode and comparing them with experimental results. Additionally, the contributions of diffusion, electromigration, electroosmotic flow, adsorption, and chemical reactions on the distribution of heavy metals were investigated based on the validated model. Furthermore, the simulation assessed the impact of a multi-electrode configuration on electric current density, pH, and the remaining concentration of Cu and Pb, as well as its role in improving removal efficiency. The results show that 45.83 % of Cu and 95.81 % of Pb were retained in the loess through adsorption. The implementation of a non-uniform electric field to increase the current density had a notable effect on enhancing the removal efficiency. In addition, for optimal performance, positioning the secondary electrodes in a cross configuration is recommended. This proposed intensification strategy underscores the potential for improving EK removal efficiency and advancing its large-scale application in the remediation of contaminated sites. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Double-confined Fe[sbnd]Co nanoalloys as efficient and stable catalyst for selective hydrogenation of nitroarenes
Abstract: Supported Co-based catalysts have shown great potential to replace noble-metal catalysts in the selective hydrogenation of substituted nitroarenes, while their tendency to deactivate during hydrogenation remains a major challenge. Here we report a facile method for constructing graphite/SiO<inf>2</inf> double-confined Fe[sbnd]Co nanoalloys, which catalyze hydrogenation of halogenated nitroarenes to halogenated anilines with high yields (> 98 %) under mild conditions. The unique double-confined structure provides effective protection for the alloy core from leaching and oxidation, leading to exceptional stability and recyclability that is unachievable by other supported or confined Co-based catalysts. Additionally, a harmonious amphiphilic environment is created to enhance the mass transport capability and to inhibit deactivation during catalytic process. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the electron-enriched graphite-layers serve as effective active sites for selective hydrogenation via a distinct mechanism, thereby improving the hydrogenation efficiency. This design concept and synthesis approach are expected to advance the development of more efficient and stable earth-abundant metal-based catalyst for selective hydrogenation catalysis. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Organic intercalation-induced interlayer engineering of V2CTx MXene for high-performance zinc-ion batteries
Abstract: Vanadium-based materials are widely explored as cathodes for aqueous zinc ion batteries (AZIBs) due to their open interlayer structure and good electrochemical properties. V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf> MXene stands out for its tunable interlayer spacing, rich redox properties, and high electrical conductivity. However, the strong electrostatic interactions between the negatively charged interlayers of V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf> MXene and Zn2+ ions hinder ion diffusion and reaction kinetics, while the multilayered structure is susceptible to interlayer collapse and material dissolution during cycling. Herein, a V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf>-TBAI<inf>3</inf> composite cathode was rationally created via the intercalation of tetrabutylammonium triiodide (TBAI<inf>3</inf>) into V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf> MXene. The organic molecule intercalation significantly expands the interlayer spacing, which not only stabilizes the layered framework but also alleviates the electrostatic attraction between V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf> MXene and Zn2+ ions. Density functional theory calculations and experimental results demonstrate that TBA+ cations interact strongly with surface oxygen atoms on V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf> MXene via electrostatic interactions, leading to localized charge redistribution. This interaction significantly enhances the d-p orbital hybridization between V 3d and O 2p orbitals, thereby reducing both the Zn2+ ions adsorption energy and migration barrier. As a result, the V<inf>2</inf>CT<inf>x</inf>-TBAI<inf>3</inf> cathode has a nearly 100 % capacity retention after 9500 cycles, exhibiting good electrochemical performance. Furthermore, the assembled pouch cells demonstrate excellent electrochemical performance and outstanding practical application capabilities. This work provides new insights into the interlayer engineering of MXene-based cathode materials and demonstrates a promising strategy for developing high-performance AZIBs. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Hydroxyl radical-exclusive Z-scheme photocatalyst for fast and complete disinfection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria-contaminated water
Abstract: Metal oxide-based photocatalysts generating reactive oxygen species are promising alternative antimicrobial reagents with antibacterial effects. Herein, we report the efficient sterilization of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) by photocatalysts exclusively producing a hydroxyl radical (•OH). The exclusive generation of •OH is manifested from the formation of a Z-scheme heterojunction between p-type (i.e., Cu<inf>2</inf>O nanoparticles, Cu<inf>2</inf>O NPs) and n-type (i.e., WO<inf>3</inf> nanowires, WO<inf>3</inf> NWs) metal oxides through the interfacial coupling of sp-sp2 conjugated carbon nanosheets (i.e., aminated graphdiyne, NH<inf>2</inf>GDY). NH<inf>2</inf>GDY prevents the oxidative corrosion of Cu<inf>2</inf>O NPs and forms a stable heterojunction with high redox potentials to exclusively generate •OH. This heterojunction photocatalyst of Cu<inf>2</inf>O-NH<inf>2</inf>GDY-WO<inf>3</inf> (CGW) reveals fast and complete antibacterial effects on Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus to achieve nearly 100% at 2 × 106 CFU/mL within 3 and 2 min, respectively, under indoor light of low power density (1.3 mW/cm2), even within 1 min under the solar light. CGW can disrupt bacterial cell walls and degrade the released DNA strands, preventing the emergence of radical-resistant bacteria. CGW maintains excellent antibacterial efficacy against ARB for over 10 recycling experiments. Therefore, the sufficient generation of •OH by efficient junctions of metal oxide-based photocatalysts leads to fast and complete purification of bacteria-contaminated water without ARB production. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: High-temperature-induced material softening formed in Ni-W-P-SiC composite coating and its wear reduction mechanism
Abstract: Electroless plating, recognized for its environmental friendliness and operational simplicity, shows great potential in various metal surface treatment applications. However, conventional nickel coatings encounter durability challenges under high contact pressures, and oxygen penetration at high temperatures. The Ni-W-P-SiC coating via electroless plating was developed in this work, which exhibited a low coefficient of friction (0.2) and retained over 50 % of its original thickness in high-load wear tests. The incorporation of W and SiC significantly improved both wear resistance and oxidation resistance. Even at high temperatures, where a wavy tribolayer formed on the surface, the Ni-W-P-SiC coating maintained superior performance. This is attributed to two key mechanisms: The formation of the Ni₃P phase increased the hardness; Its smooth surface structure effectively inhibited crack propagation. Based on the above characteristics, the composite coatings are ideally suited for metal parts operating in high-temperature and high-load environments, thereby expanding the industrial applications of electroless plating. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Chiral-driven synergistic electrolyte engineering for ultrastable aqueous zinc-ion batteries
Abstract: Electrolyte additive engineering is crucial for advancing aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs), yet stereochemical effects remain underexplored. This study systematically investigates the impact of L- and D-configured amino acids as electrolyte additives, uncovering unprecedented chiral-dependent effects on Zn2+ solvation and anode interfacial chemistry. Taking valine (Val) as a model additive, we reveal that L-Val forms a dual‑oxygen-coordinated solvation sheath with Zn2+, effectively reducing H<inf>2</inf>O activity and suppressing side reactions. In contrast, D-Val forms a mono‑oxygen-coordinated complex with limited solvation structure modification. Mechanistic insights show that L-Val preferentially adsorbs onto the Zn anode via its amino (−NH<inf>2</inf>) functional group, while outward carboxyl (-COOH) groups self-assemble into a protective layer. This architecture promotes dendrite-free Zn deposition and reversibility, achieving symmetric cell cycling stability of 5200 h (vs. 3600 h for D-Val), Zn||Cu cell Coulombic efficiency of 99.7 % over 1500 cycles, and pouch cell capacity retention of 93.2 % after 1100 cycles. These findings highlight chiral molecular engineering as a transformative strategy for electrolyte design, offering generalizable principles applicable to multivalent-ion battery systems. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Breaking activity-transport limits in photocatalysis: 3D cyanide-rich hydrogel membranes via radical polymerization for solar-powered wastewater purification
Abstract: The solar-driven degradation of organic pollutants in practical wastewater treatment is constrained not only by the intrinsic activity of photocatalysts but also by the absence of optimized catalytic systems. In this study, we devised a bifunctional K and I co-doped cyano-modified polymeric carbon nitride catalyst, which can act as a photoinitiator to enable in-situ radicals polymerization, forming a three-dimensional hydrogel photocatalytic membrane (KCN gel) under simulated sunlight. The recyclable KCN gel exhibited excellent photocatalytic performance, with the activated peroxymonosulfate (PMS) degrading organic pollutants at a rate of up to 0.438 min−1, which was 18 times higher than that of the system without PMS. Theoretical calculation reveals strong van der Waals interactions between PMS and the KCN gel, with cyanide groups identified as the key active sites for methylene blue oxidation, facilitating the generation of diverse reactive species. The KCN gel displays broad applicability, effectively abating the organic contaminant across wide concentration ranges (0.1–5.0 ppm) in simulated natural waterways, offering a promising solution for sustainable wastewater treatment. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Crystal phase engineering for polymorphic CoSe2 hollow nanoboxes with enhanced oxidase-like activity: Application in ratiometric electrochemical aptasensor for bisphenol A detection
Abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a hazardous endocrine disruptor, requires sensitive detection methods due to its widespread environmental presence and associated health risks. Herein, phase-mixed CoSe<inf>2</inf> hollow nanoboxes (m-CoSe<inf>2</inf> HNBs) with cubic and orthorhombic phases were synthesized through crystal phase engineering, which exhibited superior oxidase-like activity compared to cubic phase CoSe<inf>2</inf> hollow nanoboxes (c-CoSe<inf>2</inf> HNBs). Mechanistic investigations revealed that the enhanced oxidase-like activity of m-CoSe<inf>2</inf> HNBs stems from increased generation of reactive oxygen species (superoxide anion and singlet oxygen) and accelerated electron transfer. Utilizing the exceptional oxidase-like activity of m-CoSe<inf>2</inf> HNBs, a ratiometric electrochemical aptasensor was proposed for the determination of BPA. The ratio between the oxidation current of BPA and the electrochemical signal generated from m-CoSe<inf>2</inf> HNBs with the oxidase-like activity catalyzed oxidation of 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) was employed as a quantitative metric for BPA detection. By leveraging two independent signals, this strategy can effectively avoid interference from procedural inconsistencies and environmental fluctuations, enabling self-calibration and improving the reliability of results. Moreover, unlike electrochemical aptasensors based on peroxidase mimics, this approach eliminates the need for H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>, thereby enhancing the stability of the aptasensor. The constructed ratiometric electrochemical aptasensor exhibited a wide linear range of 0.050–15 μM, with a detection limit as low as 20 nM. It was applied to monitor BPA in real samples, yielding comparable results to those obtained using HPLC. This study offers an avenue for designing excellent oxidase mimics and determining environmental pollutants. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Energetic photoexcited electrons and enhancement of metabolic function and electron transport promote carbon chain elongation in bacterium‑cadmium sulfide biohybrid systems
Abstract: The carbon chain elongation (CE) process is essential for waste management and sustainable production of chemicals. However, gaining deeper insights into microbial metabolic regulation remains crucial for improving the CE process. Herein, photosynthetic biohybrid systems (PBSs) were developed by combining the photocatalytic semiconductor cadmium sulfide (CdS) with Clostridium kluyveri to investigate the effects of CdS synthesized via distinct routes on metabolic regulation and electron transfer mechanisms in CE process. Both PBSs incorporated with self-biosynthetic CdS (CK-BioCdS) and chemosynthetic CdS (CK-CdS) obtained higher caproate production (6.24 g/L for CK-BioCdS and 6.03 g/L for CK-CdS) and caproate selectivity (66.4 % for CK-BioCdS and 65.9 % for CK-CdS) compared to controls without CdS. Transcriptome analysis revealed that CdS significantly altered gene expression and metabolic regulation within the PBSs. The overexpression of genes encoding thiolase (thlA1) and CoA transferase (cat3) indicated that PBSs up-regulated the key genes expressions related to reverse β oxidation thus increasing caproate production. Furthermore, the differential expression of genes related to membrane-bound proteins and electron transfer suggested varied mechanisms of photoexcited electron transfer induced by CdS. These findings broaden our understanding of the diverse impacts of CdS on the regulation of bacterial metabolism and highlight the potential of PBSs for the efficient production of multi‑carbon products. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Salinity-independent evaporation: Biomimetic design of large hydrogel evaporator with 3D hierarchical channels in high-salinity brine
Abstract: In recent years, hydrogels have become popular as interfacial evaporators in solar-driven interfacial evaporation systems (SDIE) due to their excellent water absorption capacity and porous structure. However, the mechanical strength of the hydrogel-based evaporator is weak, making it susceptible to damage during long-term use. Furthermore, current research on hydrogel-based evaporators is limited in area, leading to falsely high evaporation rates due to environmental factors. In this work, a large Ti<inf>4</inf>O<inf>7</inf>-PVA waffle-shaped hydrogel (LTPWH) with 3D hierarchical biomimetic channels is developed. The LTPWH evaporator utilizes narrow band gap titanium suboxide (Ti<inf>4</inf>O<inf>7</inf>) as a photothermal absorber, with the addition of a waffle on the surface to promote Marangoni convection. This results in regional salt deposition and greatly improves salt resistance. The layered network structure generated by bionic wood serves as the support framework along with the waffle structure, significantly boosting mechanical strength and guaranteeing the stability and longevity of the extremely large area evaporator. Based on this, the LTPWH evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of 2.22 kg m−2 h−1 and an evaporation efficiency of 91.0 % in 20 wt% simulated seawater with an unprecedented area (diameter of 75 mm). It broke the limitations of brine colligative properties, as the evaporation rate in high concentration brine is even higher than that in pure water and low concentration brine. This work promotes the practical application of hydrogel-based interfacial evaporators. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Scalable ultrafast regeneration of cathodes from battery waste
Abstract: Lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO<inf>2</inf>) accounts for over 70 % of global cobalt consumption, primarily in batteries used in consumer electronics. Its conventional synthesis is energy-intensive and relies on increasingly scarce raw materials. Recycling and regeneration of LiCoO<inf>2</inf> have therefore, become critical. Existing recycling methods often involve high energy consumption, complex processing, and material loss. This work reports a hybrid thermochemical regeneration strategy integrating selective leaching, a glucose-assisted self-sustaining reaction, and brief oxidative annealing to recover high-purity LiCoO<inf>2</inf> from spent batteries. Metal nitrates extracted from spent electrodes react with glucose to form Co, CoO, and Li<inf>2</inf>CO<inf>3</inf> in minutes, followed by complete conversion to phase-pure LiCoO<inf>2</inf> at 850 °C within 10 min. These processes generate localized heat, suppress lithium volatilization, and enable ultrafast regeneration, reducing synthesis time by over 50-fold compared to conventional routes. The regenerated LiCoO<inf>2</inf> exhibits high crystallinity and electrochemical performance comparable to commercial materials at 1C, with ~100 % coulombic efficiency and stable cycling. Technometric analysis shows that the process consumes ~8 MJ/kg of feedstock and emits ~800 g CO<inf>2</inf>/kg, the lowest among existing recycling methods. Furthermore, the process yields more valuable products without the need for resynthesis, with a net economic return of ~$3690 per ton of spent LiCoO<inf>2</inf> batteries. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Tailored confinement-induced stress regulation in SnS@C anodes for enhanced lithium and sodium storage performance
Abstract: The practical application of high-capacity tin sulfide (SnS) anodes in lithium-ion (LIBs) and sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) is limited by mechanical failure. During the alloying process, SnS undergoes substantial volume expansion, which induces internal stress accumulation. This accumulated stress gradually damages the electrode structure, ultimately compromising the reversibility and stability of lithium and sodium storage. In this study, we develop a generalized “Confinement Template Evolution” strategy to synthesize double shell SnS@C anodes with tailored confinement to regulate stress accumulation within the electrodes. Through multi-scale investigations, including in-situ visualization, transmission electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and finite element simulations, we demonstrate that tailoring the carbon shell thickness of SnS@C anodes plays a critical role in mitigating stress-induced damage. The optimized carbon shells can effectively accommodate the large volume expansion associated with the formation of Li<inf>4.4</inf>Sn and Na<inf>9</inf>Sn<inf>4</inf> during the alloying process, thereby enhancing structural integrity and electrochemical stability. The SnS@C anodes feature a full-contact structure that shortens Li+/Na+ diffusion pathways, facilitating higher storage capacities. The 43 nm shell induces adaptive compressive stress for lithium storage, while the 72 nm shell accommodates stress for sodium storage. These regulations reduce the tensile stress by up to 22 % during cycling, with minimal changes in electrode thickness and enhanced reversibility and cycle performance for LIBs and SIBs. Our findings highlight that tailored confinement and stress regulation are crucial for developing high-performance anodes, providing valuab insights for next-generation electrode design. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dose-effect of ZIF-67-derived Co, N sites in carbon fibers: Optimizing Lithium deposition uniformity and Lithium sulfide precipitation capacity
Abstract: The uneven growth of lithium dendrites and the shuttling of polysulfides seriously hinder the practical application of lithium‑sulfur batteries. In this study, a three-dimensional conductive network with high-density active sites (cobalt nanoparticles and pyridine nitrogen) in Co, N@CFs composites prepared via electrospinning strategy was introduced. Increasing the ZIF-67 content (from 30 % to 90 %) markedly enhanced the specific surface area (683 m2/g) and density of the active sites, thereby suppressing dendrite growth through uniform lithium-ion flux distribution and promoting the adsorption/catalytic conversion of polysulfides. The Li//Li symmetrical battery exhibited stable cycling performance for 2500 h, with an overpotential stabilized at 30 mV. In-situ optical microscopy demonstrated that Co, N@CFs (1:0.9) effectively inhibited lithium dendrite formation, leading to uniform lithium deposition. Co, N@CFs (1:0.9) exhibited the highest adsorption capacity for Li₂S₆ and facilitated the chemical conversion of polysulfides into Li₂S, achieving a Li₂S nucleation capacity of 171.85 mAh/g. In-situ XRD analysis confirmed its optimal liquid-solid conversion efficiency, as evidenced by the significantly higher intensity of the Li₂S characteristic peak compared to low-loading samples. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Nanovaccine designed for splenic delivery augments immune responses for tumor therapy
Abstract: Spleen is an ideal secondary lymphoid organ for initiating and amplifying tumor-specific immunity; however, suboptimal antigen delivery and immune activation cause immune tolerance, limited tumor therapeutic efficacy and undesired side effects. Herein, we designed a spleen targeted nanovaccine that can carry tumor antigens and microRNA-155 (miR155) to spleen, achieving sufficient and persistent immune responses. To encapsulate miR155, we synthesized a glutathione (GSH)-responsive cationic polymer (PADDAC) that spontaneously self-assembled with miR155 to form nanocomplexes. Afterwards, the nanocomplexes were infused with tumor cell and erythrocyte membranes, granting them the ability to carry tumor associated antigens (TAAs) and target splenic antigen-presenting cells, respectively. We found that the nanovaccine demonstrated spleen-selective accumulation and efficient cytotoxic T lymphocyte activation with protective immune memory. This significantly inhibited the growth of the primary tumor and hindered the development of pulmonary metastasis in a tumor harboring mouse model. Moreover, we generated a personalized nanovaccine, which reduced local tumor recurrence post-surgery. This study highlighted the potential of splenic targeting nanovaccine for tumor preventative and therapeutic applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Selective detection and efficient recovery of Au(III) based on 1D sulfur-rich covalent organic framework
Abstract: Rising gold demand calls for sustainable extraction methods that go beyond conventional mining-dependent hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy approaches, as these traditional methods are plagued by inefficiency, high costs, and significant environmental risks. Adsorption-based methods using materials such as activated carbon or metal-organic frameworks have emerged as alternatives but face limitations in selectivity, stability, and mass transfer efficiency. This study introduces a sulfur- and nitrogen-functionalized 1D covalent organic framework (COF) with a 4-c sql topology, designed to overcome these challenges. Unlike 2D/3D COFs, the 1D structure minimizes interlayer stacking and enhances active site exposure, enabling rapid Au(III) detection (via fluorescence/colorimetric dual sensing) and in situ reduction to Au(0) without external reductants. Leveraging Au–S/N bonds and H-bonding interactions, the material achieved a low detection limit (8.5 × 10−9 M) and high adsorption efficiency in real-world scenarios, including river water and computer CPU leachates. The 1D COF's unidirectional electron channels and sulfur-rich moieties further improved selectivity and kinetics. This work demonstrates a dual-function platform for gold detection and recovery, offering a sustainable solution to mitigate e-waste hazards while advancing resource circularity. The findings highlight the potential of structurally engineered 1D COFs in precision metal recycling and environmental remediation. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Synergistic Cu0/Cu+ interface in Cu/Al2O3 catalyzes methanol steam reforming for hydrogen production
Abstract: Cu-based materials serve as the predominant catalysts for methanol steam reforming (MSR), and yet the nature of active sites and interface effects remains ambiguous due to the complexity of material surfaces. Herein, a series of xCuAl catalysts with sandwich spinel structures were synthesized in order to elucidate structure-activity relationships. The 10CuAl catalyst possesses highly dispersed Cu-O-Al spinel species at the copper‑aluminum interfaces and abundant effective Cu0-Cu+ active sites, exhibiting 93.4 % CH<inf>3</inf>OH conversion at 300 °C and the lowest apparent activation energy. To gain a deeper understanding of interface structure the formation process of xCuAl catalysts and the distribution of Cu species in the catalyst were characterized. It was found the CuAl<inf>2</inf>O<inf>4</inf> spinel in catalyst structure can sustained releases more active copper species under reduction atmosphere and provide a more utilizable interface (interface length). The results show that the effective Cu0-Cu+ interface length has a positive correlation with TOF. This study offers a fresh perspective on the design of catalysts with similar spinel structures. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Carbon nanotube/two-dimensional metal–organic framework composites with enhanced thermoelectric performances for thermoelectric generators
Abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are regarded as promising candidates for thermoelectric applications due to their excellent electrical and mechanical properties. However, their practical utility is hindered by high thermal conductivity and poor dispersion. This study explores the incorporation of two-dimensional metal–organic frameworks (2D MOFs) as additives to enhance the thermoelectric performance of CNTs. Two Zr-based 2D MOFs with distinct functional groups in their pores, namely hydrophilic ZrBTB and hydrophobic ZrBTB-BA, are employed. These 2D MOFs significantly improve the dispersion of CNTs, while the strategic selection of solvents, including 1,2-dichlorobenzene (DCB) and N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), enables precise tuning of the carrier polarity in the CNTs, thereby facilitating the development of both p-type and n-type thermoelectric composites. Notably, the CNT/ZrBTB-BA composite achieves a record-high power factor (PF) values of 395.2 and 330.8 μW m−1 K−2 for p-type and n-type thermoelectric behavior among CNT/MOF composites, respectively, accompanied by significantly enhanced figure of merit (zT) values compared to the pristine CNTs. These optimized composites are further employed to fabricate flexible thermoelectric generators, showcasing their practical potential in wearable electronics and advancing sustainable energy solutions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Self-‘cycling, boosting and propelling’ multi-functional nanoplatforms for improving tumor starvation therapy
Abstract: Starvation therapy, utilizing glucose oxidase (GOx) to deplete glucose and disrupt tumor energy, has shown promise in cancer treatment. However, this approach alone is insufficient to block ATP generation in tumors. Here, we introduce a self-‘cycling, boosting and propelling’ strategy, overcoming the ‘Achilles' heel’ of traditional starvation therapy by regulating the energy supply with CO. The high concentration of H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf> in the tumor microenvironment reacts with MnO<inf>2</inf> to generate Mn2+ and O<inf>2</inf>. Mn2+ catalyzes a Fenton-like reaction to produce hydroxyl radicals ([rad]OH) for chemodynamic therapy and T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), while O<inf>2</inf> further enhances GOx-mediated glucose consumption, producing more H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>. This process not only recycles H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf> but accelerates CO release, disrupting ATP synthesis and inhibiting tumor energy supply. Additionally, the gas released enhances nanoplatform motility, improving tumor penetration and overcoming the limited permeability of conventional nanoparticles. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated superior antitumor and antimetastatic efficacy, coupled with excellent biocompatibility. This strategy offers a promising solution to traditional starvation therapy's challenges, with strong potential for clinical translation and transformative cancer treatment. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Insights into mixotrophic metabolisms of anammox core consortia for rapid biofilm formation under low-oxygen conditions
Abstract: Anammox biofilm consortia have been documented as one effective method for biological wastewater treatment. However, the extended duration necessary for biofilm colonization poses a critical limitation to the development of stable anammox processes. This study introduced glucose supplementation at a carbon-to‑nitrogen (C/N) ratio of 0.3 in a suspended anammox system, significantly accelerating the biofilm formation. During the 120-day operational period, the intervention group exhibited a 2.65-fold biomass increment and 43.99 % enhancement in relative abundance of Ca. Kuenenia compared to controls. Multi-omics analysis revealed a cascade metabolic response wherein glucose phosphorylation via glucokinase (glk)- mediated carbon metabolism stimulated amino acid biosynthesis in anammox core consortia while maintaining functional independence from the dominant Ca. Kuenenia stuttgartiensis populations. Crucially, the resultant hydrophobic amino acids demonstrated a dual role in biofilm core and structural stabilization. This study mechanistically deciphers the effects of carbon supplementation on anammox biofilm colonization and succession, providing new insights for energy-neutral wastewater treatment aligned with carbon neutrality objectives. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Highly efficient synthesis of GO-g-wPS hybrids for improvement of mechanical properties of SIBS-based composites by tunable micromorphology
Abstract: Poly(styrene-b-isobutylene-b-styrene) triblock copolymer (SIBS) is an entirely saturated thermoplastic elastomer with an inherent microphase separation due to the thermodynamic incompatibility of hard polystyrene (PS) and soft polyisobutylene (PIB) segments. The mechanical properties are normally improved by increasing the composition of PS and molecular weight of SIBS. The high performance SIBS-based composites with a small amount (≤0.7 %) graphene oxide-graft-polystyrene (GO-g-wPS) hybrids have been prepared by construction the unique bicontinuous micromorphology and physically cross-linked 3D network. The GO-g-wPS hybrids carrying w-shaped PS chains chemically bonded on GO surfaces could be synthesized by the reaction at water/oil interface and the grafting density (G<inf>D</inf>) was effectively mediated in the range of 0.06–0.11 mmol g−1 by varying molecular weight (M<inf>n,PS</inf>) of PS precursor, reaction temperature and time. The M<inf>n,PS</inf> and G<inf>D</inf> do affect the microphase separation and homogeneous dispersion of GO sheets in the SIBS/GO-g-wPS composites. It is found that the formation of the unique bicontinuous microphase separation morphology can be mainly induced by GO-g-wPS in the composites by keeping SIBS at the same, leading to the great enhancement in mechanical properties even at a very low content of GO-g-wPS. The optimized composite of SIBS with 0.5 % of GO-g<inf>0.11</inf>-wPS<inf>7.6k</inf> behaves much higher modulus of 446 MPa, tensile strength of 24 MPa and toughness of 57 MJ m−3 than those (15.7 MPa, 14.0 MPa and 21.9 MJ m−3) of SIBS, respectively. This mechanical tunability offers a useful strategy for developing high-performance nanocomposites with potential applications in biomedical, robotics and energy fields. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Ultrafast joule heating synthesis of structurally tunable cross-linked Ni/N‑carbon fiber for enhanced CO2 electroreduction
Abstract: Electrospun nanofiber membranes serve as excellent platforms for the construction of single-atom catalysts (SACs) and self-standing electrodes, yet their practical application is limited by inter-fiber contact resistance and metal aggregation during the carbonization process. Herein, we present a rational design of three-dimensional cross-linked carbon nanofibers incorporating Ni SACs through coal tar-assisted electrospinning coupled with ultrafast joule heating. This approach effectively creates interconnected conductive networks while preserving atomic Ni dispersion and eliminating catalytically detrimental substrate defects. The optimized catalyst demonstrates exceptional CO<inf>2</inf>-to-CO conversion performance, maintaining 96 % Faradaic efficiency at industrially relevant current densities of 370 mA cm−2 with outstanding operational stability. This work offers a generalizable and scalable paradigm for manufacturing high-performance SACs electrodes for sustainable energy applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Self-driven coupling field in Fe3O4@NiFe-LDH/MnCO3 heterojunction for electrocatalytic water oxidation at high current densities
Abstract: Green hydrogen production is hindered by the sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), which involves a complex four-electron transfer and a singlet-to-triplet transition. Herein, we report a hierarchical Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@NiFe-LDH/MnCO<inf>3</inf> electrocatalyst with dual heterojunctions to synergistically couple exchange bias fields (EBF) and built-in electric fields (BIEF). The ferromagnetic Fe₃O₄ core and antiferromagnetic NiFe-LDH shell collaboratively establish an EBF-driven spin-polarization channel, enabling spin-selective electron transfer that minimizes spin scattering while facilitating triplet oxygen evolution. Concurrently, the n-n type (Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@NiFe-LDH) heterojunction combined with the p-n (NiFe-LDH/MnCO<inf>3</inf>) heterojunction generates enhanced BIEF, collectively optimizing electronic configurations and accelerating interfacial charge transfer kinetics. Benefiting from the dual-field synergy, Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@NiFe-LDH/MnCO<inf>3</inf> exhibits excellent OER performance with a low overpotential of 230 mV at 50 mA cm−2, accompanied by a Tafel slope of 73.1 mV dec−1. Moreover, the catalyst demonstrates remarkable stability for 120 h at approximately 1000 mA cm−2, confirming its practical applicability. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate that the coupled EBF-BIEF interaction lowers the d-band center of active sites while reducing the kinetic barrier for the rate-determining *OOH formation. This study pioneers the integration of spin polarization engineering with heterojunction electric field modulation, offering a universal strategy for designing high-efficiency electrocatalysts. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dispersion and mixing characteristics of slurry particles injected into a high-temperature gas-solid fluidized bed
Abstract: The dispersion and mixing of slurry particles were critical for the operation of fluidized bed, yet the underlying mechanisms remained elusive. This work investigated the dispersion and mixing characteristics of slurry particles in a quasi-2D high-temperature gas-solid fluidized bed using high-speed photography. A universal “three stages of slurry particle dispersion” was identified: agglomeration motion, disintegration, and bed diffusion, with the slurry particles initially traversing the bed, reaching the opposite sidewall, and moving with main fluidized particles, eventually achieving complete mixing. The first two stages played a crucial role in determining the dispersion rate. High injection velocity/gas velocity, central injection promoted mixing by shortening these critical stages by up to 48 %, 54 %, and 55 %, respectively. Furthermore, compared to gas-solid injection, slurry injection required a longer time for slurry particles to achieve complete mixing but improved radial dispersion. Above findings might provide guidance for the optimal operation of fluidized beds. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: PProDOS and S-doped BiOCl-modified ZnO construct flexible UV photodetectors with good stability
Abstract: In this article, a p-n heterojunction used PProDOS and ZnO nanoflowers (NFs) and perform surface modification of the ZnO NFs with S-doped BiOCl for flexible self-powered ultraviolet (UV) photodetectors. The integration of PProDOS and ZnO NFs creates an electrical field within the device, facilitating efficient dissociation of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. This, in turn, enhances the device's response speed and reduces its response time. The PProDOS structure, characterized by extended flexible chains, further contributes to superior mechanical flexibility and operational stability under bending conditions. Under standard illumination, the UV PD exhibits a high level of responsivity of 2.27 × 10−3 A/W, a detectivity of 3.29 × 1010 Jones, and rise/fall times of 0.031/0.078 s. Remarkably, It is noteworthy that even under mechanical bending, the device maintains its responsivity at 1.78 × 10−3 A/W, its detectivity at 2.72 × 1010 Jones, and its rise/fall times at 0.093/0.078 s. Additionally, the device demonstrates exceptional durability, retaining its UV detection performance after 2000 bending cycles, highlighting its potential for flexible optoelectronic applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Regulating the anchoring structure to enhance thermostability of Ru sub-nano clusters on Al-based supports for efficient C[sbnd]O bonds hydrogenolysis
Abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts with highly dispersed active metal species have found wide applications in the catalytic conversion of lignocellulosic biomass, owing to the inherent advantages in metal atom efficiency. However, it is still confronted with the challenge of developing efficient strategies to achieve enhanced thermostability of the highly dispersed metal under harsh conditions. In this work, Ru species are supported by two different aluminum-based materials (i.e., γ-AlOOH and γ-Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf>) that provide distinct anchoring sites for Ru. Complementary characterizations combined with theoretical calculations demonstrate that, compared with the triply bridging Al[sbnd]O site of γ-Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf>, the doubly bridging Al[sbnd]O site of AlOOH exhibits more intense electronic interaction with Ru species. Consequently, this doubly bridging Al[sbnd]O site as the anchoring site provides sufficient thermal resistance to immobilize the sub-nanometer Ru species under the high-temperature aging condition. The maintained high dispersion of Ru on AlOOH sustains the high activity (5.2 min−1) and selectivity (75 %) in the production of aromatics during the hydrotreating of diphenyl ether. This work may contribute to the catalyst design for manipulating the surface-anchoring structure to regulate thermostability and dispersion of supported metal catalysts. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Assessing virgin and reclaimed carbon fibre electrodes in structural batteries
Abstract: The integration of structural components with energy storage functionality is a promising pathway to attaining weight reduction in aircraft and electric vehicles. In this work, we present a structural lithium-ion full cell that utilizes a discontinuous recycled carbon fibre textile as a cathode, paired with a virgin twill-weave carbon fibre anode and embedded within an epoxy-based solid battery electrolyte (SBE) containing an LiTFSI:TEGDME solvate ionic liquid (SIL). Two carbon fibre architectures were evaluated in half-cell conditions for both the cathode and anode - a 60 GSM recycled non-woven and a 325 GSM twill-weave carbon fibre. Despite the lower mass-loading, the reclaimed non-woven carbon fibre outperformed the woven counterpart due to possessing superior ion accessibility, resin infiltration and active mass distribution. The evaluation of a hybrid full cell using a reclaimed carbon fibre cathode and twill-weave anode demonstrated stable cycling at C/20 with a specific capacity of 25 mAh g−1, fabricated entirely under ambient conditions without the need for a glovebox or dry room. This scalable prepreg-inspired approach demonstrates the feasibility of multifunctional composite design under real-world conditions, whilst also valorising reclaimed carbon fibres. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Artificial intelligence integrated three-dimensional hybrid SERS sensor towards trace level molecular detection
Abstract: The development of three-dimensional (3D) nanoengineered surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates has emerged as a powerful strategy for achieving ultrasensitive and highly selective molecular detection. In this study, chemical oxidative polymerization process was adopted to synthesize polypyrrole (PPy) nanospheres, followed by the in-situ decoration of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and subsequently integrated the 3D PPy@Au SERS material into the flexible polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane through vacuum filtration technique. This approach facilitated the formation of a high-density plasmonic network, enhancing localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) and enabling the generation of multimodal hotspots for optimized SERS performance. By integrating PPy as a functional material with AuNPs, this hybrid platform leverages synergistic electromagnetic and chemical enhancement mechanisms, optimizing both detection sensitivity and molecular specificity. The substrate achieves an enhancement factor (EF) of ∼109, allowing highly reproducible and trace-level molecular detection. This system demonstrates an ultralow limit of detection (LOD) of 10−11 M for thiram, validated through real-world testing on fruit surfaces. To further enhance detection precision and automate spectral classification, an artificial neural network (ANN) model was developed for SERS spectral analysis. The trained ANN model exhibited 100 % classification accuracy, effectively distinguishing spectral features of thiram residues from organic pollutants such as methylene blue (MB), acid orange (AO), indigo carmine (IC) and rhodamine B (RB) reinforcing its robust predictive capability for real-world sensing. This work presents a scalable 3D SERS sensing platform that combines plasmonic nanoengineering with artificial intelligence (AI) driven analysis for real-time and non-destructive molecular detection. The AI-integrated approach enhances adaptability, positioning it as a next-generation tool for food security, environmental monitoring and biomedical applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Bioleaching of valuable metals from spent lithium iron phosphate batteries using food-grade Lactobacillus acidophilus
Abstract: This study pioneers the application of Lactobacillus acidophilus (a mild acidophilic and biosafety level one bacterium) in bioleaching valuable metal from spent lithium iron phosphate batteries, expanding the microbes used in bioleaching beyond conventional strongly acidophilic bacteria. Different characterization methods as well as thermodynamic/transcriptomic analysis combined with the corresponding chemical lactic acid leaching experiment were applied to investigate the underlying bioleaching mechanisms. Results showed that a two-step bioleaching approach can leach 85.1 % Li and 59.9 % Fe at a pulp density of 2.5 g/L. The bioleaching percentage of Li decreased with increasing pulp densities (60.8 % at a pulp density of 5.0 g/L). The addition of extracellular polymeric substances increased the bioleaching rate, and enhanced selectivity of Li alongside the formation of secondary Fe-bearing phases. The biogenic lactic acid was the driving force for bioleaching. These findings provide insights into the use of mild lactic acid producing bacteria for bioleaching valuable metals from spent lithium-containing batteries. Title: Debonding in bicomponent chemical fibers
Abstract: Here, solidification and bonding of different polymers in bicomponent fibers formed by meltblowing is explored theoretically and experimentally. The two-dimensional thermoelasticity problem for typical bicomponent fiber cross-sections is posed and solved to predict the stress fields developing due to the thermal stresses emerging during fiber solidification in flight. The interfacial stresses (which can become under certain conditions disjoining and thus, potentially detrimental) between two polymers are predicted and compared to the experimentally-established critical debonding stresses, characteristic of polymer pairs of interest. The analytical benchmark problems of thermoelastic theory are based on the solutions for the thermoelastic potential and the Airy stress function. The more general and involved cases are solved numerically, while the numerical accuracy is facilitated by comparisons with the analytical benchmark cases. The critical disjoining (debonding) stresses established experimentally in the accompanying work are used to draw conclusions regarding the conditions leading to debonding and failure of bicomponent fibers. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Optimizing proton transfer of polybenzimidazole membrane through Grotthuss mechanism by an acid swelling strategy
Abstract: The dense structure of PBI contributes to its structural stability and ion selectivity, making it suitable for vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB) membranes. However, the dense structure also limits its proton transfer. This study proposes an acid swelling strategy through dense strong acid treatment to activate PBI to induce structure relaxation and enhance its proton conductivity efficiently. Through a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental characterization, it is demonstrated that the proton transfer in the acid swelled PBI membrane is enhanced by its facilitated Grotthuss mechanism through structure optimization. Additionally, the effect of treated acid properties on the activation process is unraveled. As an example of the acid swelling PBI strategy, HCOOH-PBI demonstrates significant performance improvements compared to normal PBI, its proton conductivity increases by over 2590 % from 1.93 to 50.00 mS cm−1. The assembled VRFB achieves a great energy efficiency of 76.4 % under 200 mA cm−2, comparable to that of the commercial Nafion 212. This study deeply analyzed the impact of the acid properties on the structure and performance of PBI membrane. And the simple and effective acid swelling strategy offers a promising modification approach for related fields. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Excellent dielectric energy storage properties of Pb-based antiferroelectric ceramics via phase structure regulation and grain engineering
Abstract: Lead-based antiferroelectric ceramics have demonstrated significant potential for advanced energy storage systems due to their unique field-induced phase transition characteristics. However, the inherent limitations of hysteretic losses caused by long-range polar antiferroelectric ordering in and insufficient breakdown electric strength (E<inf>b</inf>) resulting from coarse-grained microstructures severely restrict their energy storage performance. This work proposes a defect-grain synergy engineering strategy by designing (Pb<inf>0.97−x</inf>Sm<inf>0.02</inf>Sr<inf>x</inf>)(Zr<inf>0.5</inf>Sn<inf>0.5</inf>)O<inf>3</inf> ceramics. Through the synergistic effects of Sr2+ doping and grain boundary engineering, simultaneous optimization of phase transition fields and enhancement of E<inf>b</inf> are achieved. It demonstrates that Sr2+ doping enhances the stability of the antiferroelectric phase, effectively delaying the phase transition field while improving E<inf>b</inf>, thereby synergistically optimizing both energy storage density (W<inf>rec</inf>) and energy storage efficiency (η). The optimized composition (Pb<inf>0.96</inf>Sm<inf>0.02</inf>Sr<inf>0.01</inf>)(Zr<inf>0.5</inf>Sn<inf>0.5</inf>)O<inf>3</inf> exhibits exceptional performance: under an electric field of 390 kV/cm, it achieves a high energy storage density of 8.92 J/cm3. Meanwhile, it has a remarkable power density of 214.39 MW/cm3, a high current density of 1240.14 A/cm2, and an ultrafast discharge response time of 65.7 ns under 340 kV/cm. This strategy provides a new solution for designing high-performance pulse capacitors, highlighting its potential in developing next-generation energy storage applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multi-center corrosion inhibition strategy for enhanced interfacial stability and longevity of aluminum-air batteries
Abstract: Aluminum-Air batteries (AABs) suffer from anode self-corrosion and parasitic hydrogen generation. These issues markedly degrade their electrochemical performance. We introduce a novel multi-center adsorption corrosion inhibitor, 2-mercapto-3-pyridinecarboxylic acid (MPA), to mitigate these issues. Theoretical calculations reveal that MPA exhibits an adsorption energy of 1.54 eV on the Al surface, 2.5 times higher than that of H<inf>2</inf>O. This high adsorption originates from the multi-center adsorption of its sulfhydryl (-SH), carboxyl (-COOH), and pyridine groups. Experimental results demonstrate that adding 10 mM MPA to 4 M NaOH electrolyte reduces the corrosion current density by 46.1 % (from 25.37 to 13.68 mA cm−2) and suppresses the hydrogen evolution rate by 41.7 %. In-situ Fourier Transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and Time-of-Flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) analyses confirm that MPA forms a dense protective layer on the Al surface via Al-S/O/N chemical bonds. This molecular barrier stabilizes the Al anode interface and its kinetic behavior. Compared to traditional corrosion inhibitors, this interface optimization effect of MBA is more significant. As a result, the discharge cycling lifespan of AABs was extended by 1.5 times and the specific capacity was increased by 65.7 % (1379.3 mAh g−1). Molecular dynamics(MD) simulations further elucidate MPA's rapid adsorption kinetics and its ability to inhibit water penetration at the Al interface. Our findings suggest a robust multi-center adsorption strategy that enables the practical development of long-lasting, high-performance Aluminum-Air batteries to develop their commercial application. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Enhancing the thermal conductivity of carbon fiber composites by unzipping MWCNTs into GNRs through flash Joule heating
Abstract: With the advancement of high power and integrated device technologies, the issue of heat accumulation has resulted in great challenges to the packaging materials. The unsatisfied thermal conductivity is significantly limiting the application prospects of carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites. Multi-walled carbon nanotubes have been adopted as a promising thermally conductive additive as well as a supportive framework. Whereas, the multilayer structure is found to be detrimental to the effective propagation of phonons, and unzipping them into graphene nanoribbons can significantly improve the composite's thermal performance. However, the current methods for fabricating GNRs are either inefficient or environmentally unfriendly. In this paper, we propose a flash Joule heating method to unzip MWCNTs into GNRs, with characteristics of fast, convenient, economical, and environmentally friendly. Various experimental characterizations have been used to verify the production of GNRs, including Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. TGA results have indicated enhanced oxidation resistance and thermal stability for the modified CNTs. Finally, the optimized CFRP composites have been prepared, behaving significant improvements in both mechanical and thermal properties. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Engineering multifunctional carbon armor coated hierarchical porous Ni3N electrode for high-efficient alkaline seawater electrolysis to produce hydrogen
Abstract: The seawater possesses immense potential for generating carbon-neutral green hydrogen. However, the current seawater electrolysis technology is seriously hindered by the poor stability of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at cathode due to undesirable insoluble precipitates and severe corrosion in practical application. Herein, the novel hierarchical porous Ni<inf>3</inf>N coated with carbon (Ni<inf>3</inf>N@C) on 3D coarsened nickel foam (NF/Ni) was prepared via a two-step electrodeposition and annealing process. The resultant NF/Ni/Ni<inf>3</inf>N@C hybrid electrocatalyst possesses superior seawater electrolysis activity, attaining an impressively low overpotential of 84 mV at 100 mA cm−2. Moreover, benefiting from physical isolation effect of the surface carbon shell, it has excellent long-term corrosion resistance and stability at 300 mA cm−2 in seawater for 192 h. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidated that the carbon layer can reconfigure Ni<inf>3</inf>N electronic structure, effectively accelerate the water dissociation and optimize H⁎ adsorption in alkaline electrolytes as well as lower energy barriers for reaction steps. The rational optimization strategy utilizing protective carbon coating presents a prospective route to fabricate non-noble metal catalyst for sustainable molecular hydrogen production under harsh seawater environment. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Mg and Ni nanoparticles embedded in carbon scaffold for Mg-Ni@C nanocomposites with high loading and low dehydrogenation enthalpy
Abstract: The controllable preparation of ultra-small Mg nanoparticles (NP) and nanocatalysts is an effective way to improve the hydrogen storage performance of Mg-based materials. However, particles of small diameter tend to agglomeration and growth due to their high surface activity, which making it a great challenge to obtain anti-agglomeration, high loading Mg-based materials. This work prepared MgBu<inf>2</inf>@NiZn-ZIF precursor by in-situ encapsulating MgBu<inf>2</inf> precipitated by solvent displacement in NiZn-ZIF, and then obtained Mg-Ni@C-10-800 nanocomposites with 4.7 nm Mg NPs and 5.3 nm Ni nanocatalysts embedded in carbon scaffolds by pyrolysis at 800 °C. It is notable that the loading rate attains an astonishing 73.7 %. Due to the synergistic effect of nanoconfinement and nanocatalysis, Mg-Ni@C-10-800 presents remarkable hydrogen storage performance. Surprisingly, the enthalpy of hydrogen ab−/desorption significantly reduces to −59.5/60.0 kJ mol−1 H<inf>2</inf>. Mg-Ni@C-10-800 is capable of absorbing 4.6 wt% H<inf>2</inf> at 200 °C and can release 4.0 wt% H<inf>2</inf> at 250 °C, and the Ea<inf>(abs)</inf>/Ea<inf>(des)</inf> is decreased to an astonishing 40.1/65.3 kJ mol−1 H<inf>2</inf>. First principles calculations show that Mg<inf>2</inf>NiH<inf>4</inf> elongates Mg[sbnd]H bonds and promotes the hydrogen release of MgH<inf>2</inf>. This study provides a new insight into the controlled preparation of Mg NPs and catalysts, and the acquisition of high-performance Mg-based hydrogen storage materials. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Signal amplification via MOF-nanozyme microenvironment modulation in nanochannels for PFOA detection
Abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pose major environmental and health risks, yet their accurate detection in water remains challenging. This study presents an electrochemical sensing platform for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) detection via modulation of nanozyme activity in TiO<inf>2</inf> nanochannels. A Ce-based metal-organic framework (CeMOF) with peroxidase-like activity is grown on TiO<inf>2</inf> nanochannels membranes (TiNM) to form the catalytic center. A polyelectrolyte Layer-By-Layer film of poly (diallyldimethylammonium) (PDDA) and poly (styrenesulfonate) (PSS) regulates the nanochannels surface, resulting a polyelectrolyte-functionalized CeMOF-modified TiO<inf>2</inf> nanochannels membrane (TiNM-CeMOF-P). Strong hydrophobic interactions between the fluorinated chains of PFOA and the pyrrolidinium rings in PDDA displacement the PSS layer, rendering the nanochannels hydrophobic and enhancing the adsorption of oxidized 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (oxTMB), which subsequently inhibits the catalytic activity of CeMOF. Using current-voltage (I[sbnd]V) characteristics, the platform achieves a detection limit as low as 0.078 nM and a broad linear range from 0.25 nM to 1 mM. This sensing platform offers a novel approach for PFOA detection and provides the ability to differentiate between PFAS compounds with varying carbon chain lengths. The developed sensor is rapid, cost-effective, sensitive, and portable, offering a promising solution for on-site environmental monitoring and management of PFAS contamination. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Harps with directed arrangement spines enables efficient fog harvesting
Abstract: Fog harvesting presents a potential solution to freshwater scarcity, with harp structures emerging as an efficient large-scale collection method, though their reliance on passive collection mechanisms remains a limiting factor. Inspired by the unique wettability and leaf morphology of xeric organisms, this study develops a novel fog collector for large-scale water harvesting. The bioinspired design synergistically integrates dual Laplace pressure gradients and low adhesion forces to optimize droplet nucleation, growth, and shedding. A single fiber achieves a 305 % enhancement in collection efficiency under low wind velocity (≤ 2 m/s). When scaled to a composite system, the collector exhibits an exceptional fog-harvesting rate of 17.5 kg·m−2·h−1. Rigorous laboratory tests (multi-directional airflow, variable wind velocity) and field trials demonstrate its superior universality. The proposed fabrication method is simple, cost-effective, and scalable, offering new insights for designing high-performance fog collectors in low-wind environments. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Self-assembled g-C3N4/ZnO quantum dots Z-scheme heterojunction for effective photocatalytic methane oxidation to C1 oxygenates under mild conditions
Abstract: Direct photocatalytic methane conversion into high-value liquid oxygenates has garnered significant research interest under mild conditions, yet a critical challenge is to obtain an excellent formaldehyde yield rate and selectivity only using H<inf>2</inf>O as the oxidant. Herein, a 2D g-C<inf>3</inf>N<inf>4</inf> nanosheet/ 0D ZnO quantum dots (ZCN) Z-scheme heterojunction was established by the self-assembly strategy to acquire an outstanding C1 liquid oxygenates (methanol and formaldehyde) with productivity of 908.13 μmol g<inf>cat</inf>−1 h−1 under ambient temperature and pressure without extra oxidant. Notably, the HCHO yield rate could be reached to 706.32 μmol g<inf>cat</inf>−1 h−1 with a selectivity of 69 %. The confinement effect of ZnO quantum dots (ZnO QDs) broadens the bandgap to some extent, making the catalyst possess a strong oxidation potential that could oxidize H<inf>2</inf>O to generate enough hydroxyl radical (·OH) for activating CH<inf>4</inf>. Meanwhile, the ZCN Z-scheme heterostructure improves the migration and transport efficiency of photoexcitons but also enhances the activation and adsorption of CH<inf>4.</inf> In situ experiments verify that the ZCN heterostructure accelerates the generation of methyl radical (·CH<inf>3</inf>) and ·OH. This work paves a new way toward rationally constructing photocatalysts for CH<inf>4</inf> conversion into desirable chemical products under ambient conditions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Inorganic-microorganism hybrid system driven by cross-interface electron transfer: mechanism analysis and research progress on waste resource utilization
Abstract: Inorganic materials-anaerobic microorganism hybrid systems have become a breakthrough platform for environmental and energy applications. By utilizing the synergistic effects between abiotic and biotic components, these systems achieve remarkable efficiency in pollutant degradation, resource conversion, and energy recovery. This paper systematically reviews the construction strategies and cross-interface synergistic mechanisms of such hybrid systems, classifying them into three categories: suspended mixed, microbial self-synthesis, and intracellular bound, while also summarizing compatible anaerobic microorganisms. The key interaction processes between inorganic materials and microorganisms are analyzed in depth, focusing on interfacial electron transfer mechanism, metabolic environment regulation, community function enhancement, and directional control of electron flow. At the application level, this paper summarizes the innovative progress of the system in semi-artificial photosynthesis, biological hydrogen production, wastewater treatment, and organic waste anaerobic digestion, highlighting its strategic value for sustainable environmental technologies. Finally, this paper proposes key challenges that need to be paid attention to in the future, such as precise material function modulation, mechanistic interface studies, and scalable system integration, to provide theoretical foundations and development pathways for interdisciplinary advances and practical implementation in this field. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Nanobubbles as pore-forming agents in non-solvent induced phase separation of polysulfone ultrafiltration membranes
Abstract: In this study, we present a new approach for increasing the surface porosity of polysulfone (PSU) ultrafiltration (UF) membranes formed via nonsolvent induced phase separation (NIPS) using nanobubbles (NB) dispersed in the nonsolvent as pore forming agents. A series of UF membranes were hand-casted with and without NBs in an aqueous nonsolvent bath using different concentrations of PSU. We compared the structure and performance of NB-enhanced UF membranes with a number of other well-known methods for increasing NIPS-UF membrane porosity. Analysis of scanning electron microscope (SEM) images enabled quantification of surface porosity, pore size distribution, and mean pore size, while data from filtration experiments established the apparent water permeance, solute rejection, and mean pore size of all membranes. The inclusion of NBs in the nonsolvent bath enhanced the body porosity, total thickness, and surface porosity compared to membranes formed identically, but without NBs. Hence, NBs universally increased water permeability. Although NBs were on average about 80 nm in the aqueous solution, they produced pores on the average of 17 nm. So, NBs enhanced water permeability without sacrificing rejection for membranes with average pore radius at or above 17 nm; however, for membranes with average pore radius below 17 nm, water permeability increased with decreasing solute rejection. NBs offer several potential advantages over conventional approaches to increase surface porosity, such as: (1) no need for additional pore-forming chemicals, heat, or solvents/nonsolvents, and (2) improved precision in fine-tuning separation performance of NIPS membranes. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Chemically robust ether-free polymer-based bipolar membrane with a 3D junction for high-performance water splitting and efficient acid/base production
Abstract: In this study, ether-free poly(5-Bromoisatin-co-p-Terphenyl) was synthesized to prepare two ion-exchange polymers derived from a single polymer backbone, with the aim of optimizing the synthesis process of ionomers and leveraging the chemical stability of the ether-free polymer to develop high-performance bipolar membranes (BPMs) with high chemical stability. The anion-exchange (AEM) and cation-exchange (CEM) membranes prepared using the two ion-exchange polymers demonstrated an ion exchange capacity (IEC) of 1.8 meq g−1, swelling ratios ranging from 9.4%–16.6% and 5.0%–6.5%, and water uptake values of 21.3%–49.8% and 15.2%–17.6% from 30 °C to 80 °C, respectively. More importantly, the ether-free AEM and CEM effectively prevent mass loss over four weeks in 4 M NaOH and H<inf>2</inf>SO<inf>4</inf> at a level of 4%–5%. To additionally endow an ether-free BPM with structural stability and high water-splitting efficiency, dual electrospinning (DE) was used to prepare BPMs (3D-BPM) with a 3D junction, which can provide an interlocking effect to prevent delamination, a large interfacial area available for water splitting, and better pathways for the diffusion of water molecules and water dissociation product ions. The optimized BPM (i.e., DE1), featuring a 3D junction layer constituting 25% of the total membrane thickness, achieved a water-splitting voltage of 1.38 V and transmembrane voltage (TMV) of 2.2 V at 100 mA/cm2, corresponding to almost half of those of a 2D-BPM (i.e., DE0) prepared using the same ion-exchange polymers. Also, DE1 exhibited exceptional acid-base production efficiency, with a current efficiency of 85.2%, which was about 6%p higher than DE0, while decreasing the energy consumption (4.32 kWh/kg) by 8.5% compared to DE0. This work highlights that the ether-free 3D-BPM can achieve chemical/structural stability and high water-splitting capability simultaneously. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Pushing boundaries: Nature-inspired hybrid microstructured flexible sensors with enhanced detection range
Abstract: Flexible pressure sensors have garnered significant interest due to their potential applications in human motion monitoring, human-machine interfaces, and diverse applications a wide range of other uses. However, striking a balance between high sensitivity and wide detection range using cost-effective and simple fabrication methods remains a serious challenge. Bio-inspired microstructure design provides a new solution to this limitation. Herein, we introduce a bio-templated strategy using desiccated orange peel to replicate its hierarchical surface textures, fabricating a flexible piezoresistive sensor with a dual-scale architecture of spherical protrusions and multilevel wrinkles. These bioengineered microstructures enhance both sensitivity and dynamic range. To mitigate signal saturation caused by full microstructural compression under extreme stress, we developed an adaptive compensation mechanism leveraging tunneling effect in conductive networks, extending linear responsivity beyond traditional structural limits. Systematic testing demonstrates the sensor's high sensitivity (839.1 kPa−1), broad detection range (>2000 kPa), rapid response/recovery (none of them are exceeds 80 ms), and durability (10,000 cycles). Applications in wearable health monitoring, voice recognition, and smart road monitoring systems validate its versatility. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Hierarchical porous MOF/PEDOT:PSS films with enhanced mechanical properties and thermoelectric performance
Abstract: Efficient waste heat recovery via thermoelectric materials offers a promising way to boost energy efficiency, making performance enhancement strategies crucial in thermoelectric research. Here, we propose an effective synergistic optimization strategy for thermoelectric materials, focusing on enhancing mechanical properties, reducing thermal conductivity, and improving Seebeck coefficients. To achieve this, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with alkaline and amphoteric groups are synthesized and incorporated into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) to fabricate UiO-66-NH<inf>2</inf>/PEDOT:PSS (UNPP) and UiO-66-NH-SO<inf>3</inf>H/PEDOT:PSS (UNSPP) composite films. The electrostatic interactions between MOFs and PEDOT:PSS significantly reinforce the mechanical properties of UNPP and UNSPP. Furthermore, due to the isolation and “dragging effect” of MOFs on flexible PEDOT: PSS chains during the drying process, UNPP and UNSPP films exhibit hierarchical porous structures, achieving ultra-low thermal conductivity of 0.021 and 0.042 W·m−1·K−1 respectively, with the former, to the best of our knowledge, being the lowest reported value for PEDOT:PSS-based thermoelectric films. Additionally, MOF doping influences carrier transport within the composite films, leading to an improved Seebeck coefficient of up to 30.8 μV·K−1. The UNSPP show a maximum ZT of 0.263. This work presents an innovative strategy for efficient synergistic optimization of MOF/PEDOT:PSS films, highlighting their potential in wearable electronics and waste heat recovery. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Regulation of Li-ion flux by metal organic framework in compact quasi-solid-state electrolyte for wide-temperature lithium-metal batteries
Abstract: The practical application of lithium metal anodes is hindered by uncontrolled growth of lithium dendrites, which can ulteriorly exacerbate at low or high temperature. To address these issues, a dense quasi-solid-state electrolyte (CPLZ) operating at wide-temperature-range is prepared based on cellulose acetate (CA) and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) as polymer matrices, metal organic framework (ZIF-8) as nanofiller, LiTFSI as Li-ion source. The Raman spectra confirms the strong interaction between ZIF-8 and TFSI− and FTIR spectra verifies ZIF-8 weakens the adsorption of Li+ on CA, which can promote Li salt dissociation, accelerate the Li+ transport and regulate the Li+ flux, thereby facilitating uniform lithium deposition. Meanwhile, the addition of ZIF-8 greatly improves dendrite suppression by enhancing CPLZ's mechanical strength. The obtained CPLZ electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity over a wide temperature range (6.9 × 10−4 S cm−1 at room temperature), a high ion migration number (0.57 at room temperature) and achieves the stable and reversible lithium deposition and stripping over 400 h. Furthermore, the assembled Li|CPLZ|LiFePO<inf>4</inf> cells exhibit the discharge-capacity of 133.9 mA h g−1 at 3C after 400 cycles at room temperature. Most importantly, thanks to high ion transport and interface stability, the Li|CPLZ|LiFePO<inf>4</inf> batteries exhibit an excellent wide-temperature-range operation with stable cycling over 500 cycles with the discharge-capacity of 138.1 mA h g−1 at 1C at 60 °C and the capacity retain up to 60 % of room temperature at −15 °C. This research provides valuable insights for advancing lithium metal batteries characterized by enhanced safety and prolonged cycle stability at wide-temperature-range. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Optimal retrofit of extractive distillation to hybrid distillation/crystallization scheme: Modeling and validation
Abstract: Hybrid distillation/crystallization processes present a promising approach for energy and cost savings in separating close-boiling mixtures. This study developed a design and optimization framework for retrofitting a conventional 2-methylnaphthalene extractive distillation sequence into a hybrid scheme. A multi-objective optimization strategy using the non-dominated sorted genetic algorithm-III algorithm minimizes total annual cost (TAC) and CO₂ emissions via the Python-Aspen Plus platform. The optimization results showed that TAC and CO<inf>2</inf> emissions were reduced by 14.62 % and 10.04 % in terms of the conventional extractive distillation. A simulation-based method for predicting melt crystallization product purity and yield was experimentally validated, showing <0.1 % purity deviation from predictions. The hybrid distillation/crystallization process achieved enhanced purity and 0.72 % lower CO₂ emissions versus the optimized extractive distillation process. This work advances eco-efficient separation systems by integrating crystallization and predictive modeling of critical quality attributes, offering significant potential for sustainable multicomponent separation processes. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Facile synthesis of 2D “GO”-TiO₂ @biochar hybrid nanocomposites for synergistic adsorption and photocatalytic elimination of veterinary antibiotics from livestock effluents
Abstract: Veterinary practices in livestock farming have resulted in widespread antibiotic contamination, notably involving enrofloxacin (ENR), oxytetracycline (OTC), and sulfamethoxazole (SMX) in effluents, triggering severe impacts on aquatic biodiversity and posing dangers to public well-being. This work reports a multifunctional nanocomposite consisting of graphene oxide, biochar, and TiO<inf>₂</inf> (GBT) tailored for combined adsorption and photocatalytic elimination of these antibiotics. GBT composites with varying TiO<inf>₂</inf> loadings (5 %, 10 %, 20 %) were fabricated through a combination of biomass pyrolysis, an economically enhanced graphene oxide synthesis protocol optimized for biochar integration, and a modified sol-gel process for TiO<inf>₂</inf> deposition. This integrated strategy was more cost-effective and efficient than conventional methods for producing biochar-based composite materials. Comprehensive material characterizations confirmed high surface area, functional group richness, and homogeneous distribution of GO and TiO<inf>₂</inf> within the porous biochar framework. Among the variants, GBT-10 exhibited the best performance, achieving >95 % removal of all three antibiotics under UV irradiation while retaining over 89 % efficiency after five reuse cycles. Adsorption kinetics followed pseudo-second-order behavior, while equilibrium data aligned with the Freundlich isotherm, indicating heterogeneous multilayer adsorption. Mechanisms included π−π interactions, hydrogen bonding, pore-entrapment, and photocatalytic oxidation facilitated by reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly effective at pH 5–8. Comparative assessments revealed that GBT-20 had faster kinetics but suffered from pore blockage, while GBT-5 had lower active site density. Overall, GBT-10 offers a cost-effective, scalable platform for mitigating pharmaceutical contaminants in livestock wastewater, supporting sustainable water treatment and circular resource recovery goals. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
