Title: Enhancing nitrate reduction reaction electroactivity of Fe single atom catalyst by modification of Fe nanoclusters and further application in self-powered ammonia synthesis from air
Abstract: Designing cost-effective nitrate reduction reaction (NO<inf>3</inf>RR) electrocatalysts and exploring a clean and sustainable energy as power to drive this process are of great significance for the sustainability of the nitrogen cycle. Herein, by direct pyrolysis of MOF and g-C<inf>3</inf>N<inf>4</inf>, an efficient electrocatalyst with Fe nanoclusters (Fe<inf>NC</inf>) modified Fe single atoms (Fe<inf>NC</inf>/Fe-N<inf>x</inf>) was prepared for NO<inf>3</inf>RR. Characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that the Fe<inf>NC</inf> effectively regulates the d-band structure of Fe sites, increasing the electron occupation in d<inf>z2</inf> orbital to optimize the bond order (BO) for intermediates, thus lowering the energy barrier of rate-determining step (RDS: NHO⁎ + H+ + e− → N⁎ + H<inf>2</inf>O). Therefore, the Fe<inf>NC</inf>/Fe-N<inf>x</inf> exhibits remarkable NO<inf>3</inf>RR performance with a high faradaic efficiency (FE) of 93.6 % at −0.9 V vs. RHE and an excellent NH<inf>3</inf> yield rate of 30.87 mg h−1 mg<inf>cat</inf>−1 at −1.1 V vs. RHE. Based on these, an updated triboelectric nanogenerator-based self-powered NH<inf>3</inf> synthesis system was presented, and a high rate of 22.66 μg h−1 was achieved directly using air as the raw material. This work provides a simple strategy to enhance NO<inf>3</inf>RR performance of Fe-N<inf>x</inf> electrocatalysts, and further demonstrates a smart and sustainable way for NH<inf>3</inf> synthesis. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Nitrogen/boron co-doped carbon derived from coal liquefaction residue for capacitive energy storage
Abstract: The rational structural design of heteroatom-doped porous carbon materials serves as an effective strategy for improving capacitive energy storage. Herein, three-dimensional (3D) N/B dual-doped porous carbons were prepared via a self-assembly process followed by an activation method, using asphaltenes in coal liquefaction residue (CLR) and sodium lignosulfonate (LS) as the carbon source, with urea and boric acid serving as the sources for N and B doping, respectively. These components initially self-assemble into a 3D interlinked framework via intermolecular interactions, which effectively prevents the oriented stacking of asphaltene molecules induced by π−π interactions during the carbonization process. Furthermore, it facilitates KCl/K<inf>2</inf>CO<inf>3</inf> in adequately interacting with carbon-unstable regions. Following KCl/K<inf>2</inf>CO<inf>3</inf> activation, the resulting porous carbon materials present well-developed porosity for efficient ion transport, superior conductivity for effective electron transport, and appropriate B, N heteroatom active sites for enhanced capacitance. The optimal porous carbon (NBPC800) shows a specific capacitance of 272 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 in 1 M H<inf>2</inf>SO<inf>4</inf> electrolyte. A maximum energy density of 16.9 Wh kg−1 at 200 W kg−1 is achieved by the symmetric device fabricated in 2 M Na<inf>2</inf>SO<inf>4</inf>, accompanied by remarkable cycling stability. Additionally, when used in zinc-ion hybrid capacitors (ZICs), NBPC800 possesses a high energy density of 77.35 Wh kg−1 at 160 W kg−1 with great rate performance. Theoretical calculations (DFT) reveal that N/B dual-doping contributes to an enhanced adsorption energy of electrolyte ions and improved electronic conductivity, resulting in superior electrochemical performance. This work provides N/B dual-doped porous carbons through a facile and low-cost approach for advanced energy storage applications. Moreover, it promotes the efficient and high-value utilization of coal liquefaction residue. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Self-healing, antibacterial bilayer hydrogel phase-change composites for sustainable and energy-effective cold chain logistics
Abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable and secure large-scale cold chain logistics underscores the critical need for advanced multifunctional systems to ensure energy-efficient transportation of temperature-sensitive products. Here, an innovative bilayer hydrogel phase-change composite is engineered to address this challenge. The composite features two distinct functional layers: (1) a low-thermal-conductivity outer layer composed of a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAM/SA) network integrated with NaCl solution, Zn2+ ions, and tannic acid (TA) (denoted as PSN–Zn/TA hydrogel), and (2) a high-thermal-conductivity inner layer consisting of PSN–Zn/TA hydrogel and expanded graphite. Within this system, the NaCl solution delivers a high cold-energy-storage capacity (173.7 J g−1) for precise temperature regulation, while the PAM/SA dual-network ensures structural integrity by immobilizing the solution. Zn2+ coordination imparts autonomous self-healing capabilities, and TA provides robust antibacterial activity. Strategically combining these layers generates a gradient thermal insulation effect, significantly delaying heat transfer from ambient environments. A prototype cold chain logistics device based on this hydrogel demonstrates exceptional temperature control performance comparable to conventional refrigerators, effectively preserving model temperature-sensitive compounds such as penicillin G and streptomycin. By synergizing high energy efficiency, recyclability, and multifunctionality, this bilayer hydrogel offers a scalable, sustainable solution for next-generation cold chain logistics, bridging the gap between operational efficiency and environmental responsibility. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Confined voltage stabilizers into hard segment of polyurethane for soft dielectric elastomers with enhanced electroactuation performance
Abstract: Dielectric elastomer (DE) materials hold promise as artificial muscles due to their ability to deform under external electric field stimulation. To enhance their actuation performance, we have improved the dielectric breakdown strength of polyurethane (PU) based DE materials by incorporating voltage stabilizers into their hard segment through copolymerization. Voltage stabilizers with a lower HOMO-LUMO energy gap can effectively capture high-energy electrons, thereby mitigating the degradation of polymer molecular chains and increasing the dielectric breakdown strength. Specifically, when 50 % of the hard segments in PU contain a kind of voltage stabilizer (4,4′-dihydroxybenzophenone, DHBP), the PU exhibits the optimized dielectric breakdown strength, increasing from an initial value of 32 V/μm to 58 V/μm. Notably, the modified PU retains a low initial modulus (0.24 MPa) without experiencing the stiffening problem, as the rigid structure of the DHBP is incorporated into the hard segments of PU. Without pre-stretching, the 50 % DHBP-PU achieves an improved maximum actuation strain of 57 % and a theoretical energy density of 14.4 J/m3 at 83 V/μm, outperforming most PU-DE materials. The DHBP-PU, characterized by its enhanced dielectric breakdown strength and improved electroactuation performance, holds great potential for applications in flexible actuators and soft robotics. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: CFD simulation study on the effects of inclined and rolling motions on the liquid flow distribution of tridimensional rotational flow sieve tray
Abstract: As a tray structure capable of intensifying the mass transfer process, the tridimensional rotational flow sieve tray (TRST) holds promising applications in the separation and purification of offshore multiphase flow reactors. This study investigates the influence of rolling motion on liquid flow characteristics in TRST through combined experimental and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) approaches. The hydrodynamic performance of TRST was comparatively evaluated against vortex trays and sieve trays under inclined and rolling conditions, demonstrating its superior stability and liquid distribution characteristics. TRST exhibits favorable resistance performance and maintains high-quality liquid distribution under inclined conditions. Under rolling motion, vortex trays and sieve trays exhibit high and significantly fluctuating pressure drops, whereas TRST demonstrates excellent stability due to the rotational-perforated coupled flow and centrifugal force, which effectively counteract uneven liquid distribution induced by rolling motion. In contrast, vortex and sieve trays display pronounced gas-liquid maldistribution under identical conditions, leading to diminished lateral liquid uniformity. Furthermore, CFD simulation results show high consistency with experimental data, validating model accuracy. Analysis of the liquid maldistribution factor under varied operating conditions further reveals TRST application potential in marine environments, particularly its advantages in enhancing mass transfer efficiency and reducing energy consumption. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dual photoelectric-photothermal effects synergistically overcome the cryogenic limits of aqueous supercapacitors
Abstract: While photoelectric and photothermal enhancements individually improve energy storage, their isolated use fails to resolve the coupled challenges of sluggish charge transfer and electrolyte freezing in cryogenic energy storage. Here, we pioneer a cooperative photoelectric-photothermal strategy that synergistically resolves these coupled limitations in aqueous supercapacitors. By engineering a ZnO/ZnCo<inf>2</inf>O₄ heterojunction cathode and a TiN-integrated activated carbon anode, we demonstrate a self-sustaining energy storage system working at low temperature. Under 0.35 W cm−2 light illumination, the device achieves 27.8 Wh kg−1 at −30 °C. It is 3475 % higher than its dark-operation counterpart—while retaining 64.7 % of its room-temperature capacity (43.0 Wh kg−1). It further breaks the −40 °C operational limit with 7.3 Wh kg−1, the lowest temperature achieved for aqueous supercapacitors. Systematic characterization reveals that the photothermal component effectively mitigates aqueous electrolyte freezing while the photoelectric heterojunction facilitates charge transfer kinetics, establishing a self-sustaining mechanism for low-temperature operation. This synergistic engineering approach opens new frontiers for developing high-performance energy storage devices in polar and aerospace applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: From melt-spinning to smart fabrics: Decoding α to β transformation mechanisms for high-performance piezoelectric PVDF
Abstract: Flexible piezoelectric sensors exhibit significant potential for applications in human motion monitoring, human-computer interaction, and intelligent robots, attributed to their self-powered nature and simplified wearable architecture. In addition to the developed sensitivity and output voltage of piezoelectric sensors, large-scale production is a critical prerequisite for their widespread commercialization. In this study, we report a novel method of preparing piezoelectric smart PVDF fabric via melt spinning and post-stretching. The transformation mechanism from nonpolar α phase to polar β phase over a wide temperature range (80–130 °C) was thoroughly investigated using WAXD, DSC and FTIR techniques. The findings reveal an inverse relationship between stretching temperature and phase-transformation kinetics: higher temperatures notably slow down the α to β crystal conversion, necessitating larger tensile strain for achieving comparable transformation degrees. Furthermore, multi-step destruction of the α crystal at high temperatures was observed, with preferential damage to (100) and (110) crystallographic planes before (020) and (021) planes that exhibited greater stability. Based on these insights, optimal post-stretching temperatures were determined for fabricating PVDF fiber. As demonstrated, piezoelectric generators assembled by PVDF fabric show exceptional performance, including piezoelectric output (26.3 V), high sensitivity (0.167 V/kPa), short response time (T<inf>r</inf> = 30 ms, T<inf>f</inf> = 34 ms), and long-term stability (>2000 cycles), making them ideal self-powered sensor for multimodal intelligent biomonitoring of human movement and handwriting monitor. This research provides a cost-effective and facile pathway for the scalable fabrication of high-performance, flexible, wearable piezoelectric sensors. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Tuning liganded nanocrack geometry for dynamic regulation of host macrophages
Abstract: Topographical cracks in native tissues such as brain, skin, and bone dynamically remodel across geometries to maintain tissue homeostasis. Disruptions in interactions between crack features (e.g., width and depth) and cells can impair immune responses, leading to disorder development, such as eczema, psoriasis, and angiogenesis defects. While topographical crack geometries across various scales regulate immune cell responses, precise and dynamic tuning of nanocrack geometries at tens-of-nanometers scale, critical for understanding molecular interactions between cells and extracellular matrix that dictate integrin responses, remains elusive. Herein, nanocracked materials exhibiting topographical cracks with widths tuned at integrin-presenting filopodia scale are developed by modifying hydrophobic properties of bicontinuous microemulsions, featuring magnetically responsive liganded crack-modulatable particles (CMPs) via elastic polymer linkers. CMPs can be dynamically modulated by magnetic field application, enabling transitions between deep and shallow crack states to regulate macrophage integrin recruitment, adhesion, and polarization. Narrow cracks (50 nm), smaller than filopodia, restrict infiltration and limit integrin engagement, whereas Wide cracks (110 nm) promote strong adhesion. Moderate cracks (80 nm) allow minimal adhesion in deep crack state but significantly enhance integrin recruitment upon magnetic activation to shallow crack state, facilitating macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. This is the first demonstration of dynamic nanocrack system for host cell regulation. This breakthrough offers new insights into the role of hierarchical crack architectures in regulating immunomodulation, regenerative medicine, and wound healing. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Self-powered drifting buoy for maritime anomaly traffic monitoring via electromagnetic-triboelectric coupling
Abstract: Enhancing maritime anomaly traffic monitoring is vital for national security, combating smuggling, and preventing human trafficking. In this work, we designed a self-powered drifting buoy (SDB) based on electromagnetic-triboelectric coupling for maritime anomaly traffic monitoring. The buoy shell adopts a self-righting structure combined with a low center of gravity to prevent capsizing and enable rapid self-righting. The integrated electromagnetic generator (EMG) within the SDB achieves self-powering functionality, eliminating the need for battery replacement or external power sources. In addition, the built-in corrective magnet establishes the SDB's directional reference at sea. Four integrated triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) sensors detect wave directions through voltage generated during wave-induced tilting. Coupled with built-in satellite positioning and wireless communication modules, the SDB achieves real-time monitoring and transmission of wave directions and geographical positions to coastal terminals. By deploying multiple buoys as a networked array, coastal terminals can comprehensively analyze real-time vessel positions, moving directions, and speeds through wave data transmitted from each node. This buoy-based monitoring approach provides a novel self-powered solution for maritime traffic monitoring and management. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Defect-rich carbon nanofiber membranes as metal-free catalysts for flow-through peroxymonosulfate activation: toward efficient antibiotic removal and water remediation
Abstract: Recent advancements in metal-free powder catalysts for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation have demonstrated considerable potential for water pollutant treatment. However, their practical application faces challenges in catalyst recovery and continuous operation. To address these challenges, we developed a novel porous carbon nanofiber membrane with enhanced PMS catalytic activity via a facile electrospinning process using polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and sodium lignosulfonate (SL), followed by pre-oxidation and carbonization. SL serves a dual role as both a carbon source and an activator, decomposing at elevated temperatures to generate sodium salts and gaseous byproducts. A continuous flow catalytic system was designed to evaluate the PMS activation performance of these self-supporting carbon membranes for the oxidative degradation of ciprofloxacin hydrochloride (CIP). Characterization results revealed that membranes carbonized at 900 °C exhibited superior catalytic activity, attributed to their high specific surface area, increased oxygen content, and abundant structural defects, which collectively contribute to the proposed PMS activation mechanism. Furthermore, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis was employed to identify degradation sites and elucidate potential CIP degradation pathways. This study demonstrates the promising application of metal-free carbon nanofiber membranes in sustainable water treatment technologies, offering a scalable and environmentally friendly solution for antibiotic wastewater remediation. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Enhancing power output of solar-driven evaporation electric generator through ion behavior regulation
Abstract: An evaporation-driven generator shows promise in addressing freshwater-energy shortages, but limited electric output due to slow ion transport hinders its use. We present a new generator system integrating a photothermal conversion layer and electricity-generating layer on a porous sponge skeleton, enhancing water evaporation and electricity generation simultaneously. By incorporating zero-dimensional carbon dots (CDs) and monovalent cations into the electricity-generating layer made of polyelectrolyte-based hydrogels, we improve the generator device's electricity output without compromising solar water evaporation. The electric generator achieves a threefold increase in current output by leveraging the synergistic effect of CDs and monovalent cations in ion transfer within the hydrogels. With optimized parameters, our electric generator generates a short-circuit current of 120.31 μA and an evaporation rate of 1.75 kg·m−2·h−1 under one sun irradiation. Connecting multiple SEG units in series and parallel produces high voltage and current to power electronic devices directly. This study offers an efficient and cost-effective approach for developing solar-driven water-electricity cogeneration systems. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Uncovering the critical role of cation vacancies in bronze-type VO2(B) towards enhanced electrochemical storage of mono/multi-valent cations
Abstract: Defects engineering is a promising strategy to realize enhanced mono/multi-valent cations storage in pseudocapacitive material VO<inf>2</inf>(B), however, the mechanistic understanding of mono/multi-valent cations' storage behaviors in VO<inf>2</inf>(B) is still vague, which greatly hinders its practical application. In this study, a novel “Ion doping + Selective etching” strategy has been employed to enable facile and controllable creation of cation vacancies in VO<inf>2</inf>(B) nanobelts. More importantly, the effects of cation vacancies on Na+, Mg2+, Zn2+ and Al3+ ions storage in VO<inf>2</inf>(B) have been clearly elucidated via systematic structural characterizations, theoretical calculations and electrochemical analysis. Zn2+ insertion leads to partial phase transformation of VO<inf>2</inf>(B) to Zn<inf>3</inf>(OH)<inf>2</inf>V<inf>2</inf>O<inf>7</inf>·2H<inf>2</inf>O, in which case the cation vacancies mainly promote charge transfer and provide ion storage sites rather than affect the ion diffusion process. In comparison, the incorporation of cation vacancies is beneficial in facilitating ion diffusion, charge transfer and provide abundant ion storage sites upon Na+, Mg2+ and Al3+ ions storage, thus leads to improved capacitance and rate/cycling capability. In general, this work provides valuable insights in understanding the behaviors of mono/multi-valent cations upon insertion into defective VO<inf>2</inf>(B), which also enables rational design of defect structures in other metal oxide frameworks towards enhanced electrochemical charge storage capability. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multiscale response mechanisms of the anammox system under acute sulfadiazine exposure: From EPS defense to intracellular stress
Abstract: Sulfadiazine (SDZ), a widely used sulfonamide antibiotic, is frequently detected in various wastewater sources due to its high environmental persistence. Residual SDZ accumulation in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) poses a potential threat to critical microbial processes such as anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox). However, the acute response mechanisms of anammox systems to SDZ exposure remain unclear. This study systematically elucidated the multiscale effects of acute SDZ exposure on anammox by integrating kinetic modeling, spectroscopy, molecular docking, and structural equation modeling (SEM). Results showed a concentration-dependent inhibition of anammox activity. At 5 mg/L SDZ, nitrogen removal performance was maintained through multilayered synergistic defenses, including preservation of the extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) barrier, enhanced electron transport system activity (ETSA), and upregulated antioxidant enzyme activity. At higher concentrations, SDZ accelerated EPS structural deterioration and facilitated its cellular penetration. Spectroscopic evidence confirmed the selective interaction of SDZ with proteinaceous components (PN) in EPS, inducing conformational and surface charge alterations. Molecular docking further revealed spontaneous interactions between SDZ and both substrate transporters and antioxidant enzymes. SEM analysis revealed that EPS degradation exerted a direct inhibitory effect on anammox activity, while ROS had a weaker indirect impact. Moreover, EPS also modulated the antioxidant system, highlighting its dual role as both a structural shield and biochemical regulator. This study reveals the spatially stratified damage pathway of SDZ and underscores the central role of EPS in anammox resilience. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Biomineralized flexible metal nanofilms with surface plasmon resonance for adhesion of heterogeneous materials
Abstract: Flexible substrates with metal deposition layers are widely used in the fabrication of wearable devices. However, metal deposition processes are often complex and unsatisfactory due to the multifaceted interplay between deposition conditions and substrate properties. Therefore, it is crucial to find a convenient and effective method to improve the bonding between flexible substrates and metal interfaces. In this study, a phase transition protein-induced gold mineralization strategy is proposed to enhance the metal-substate interactions by facilitating gold deposition onto flexible substrates adhered with phase transition proteins. The self-assembly and conformational adaptation of phase transition proteins (including lactalbumin, lysozyme, and bovine serum albumin) driven by disulfide bond cleavage, provide abundant binding sites and stabilize the structure, enabling the reliable mineralization of gold ions on flexible substrates. The resulting gold-modified flexible substrates maintain the inherent flexibility of the original materials while manifesting excellent surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) properties, reproducibility, and mechanical durability, exhibiting compatibility with various substrates, which can be applied for the detection of methotrexate in urine with a wide range from 10−8 to 10−3 M. This research provides a biomimetic approach to optimize metal adhesion on flexible materials and contributes to the development of biocompatible and stable metal-coated flexible materials. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Reactive oxygen species generation induced by coupling Phanerochaete chrysosporium with intermittent micro-aeration to enhance methane production
Abstract: Anaerobic digestion is constrained by the rate-limiting step of hydrolysis and acidogenesis of macromolecular organic matter, which significantly affects the overall process efficiency and system stability. This study introduced aerobic fungi Phanerochaete chrysosporium into an anaerobic digestion system combined with intermittent micro-aeration to induce the generation of extracellular reactive oxygen species, thereby accelerating the decomposition of organic solid waste and promoting methane production. The results showed that under an optimal aeration intensity of 8 % (V<inf>Aeration</inf>:V<inf>Reactor</inf>)/day, the intermittent micro-aeration (IMA) group enhanced cumulative methane production by 17.22 %, while the combined application of IMA with P. chrysosporium (IMA-P) group increased by 26.36 %, both relative to the non-aerated control group lacking P. chrysosporium supplementation. The implementation of intermittent micro-aeration induced periodic oscillations in oxidation-reduction potential, ranging from −460 mV to −300 mV, which subsequently triggered the generation of •OH at concentrations between 35.84 μM and 65.29 μM. Under the limited oxygen condition, P. chrysosporium secreted lignocellulolytic enzymes and enhanced •OH generation to accelerate the degradation of lignocellulose. Microbial community analysis revealed that P. chrysosporium could proliferate in the anaerobic digester under such intermittent micro-aeration conditions. The enrichment of methanogens capable of coping with O<inf>2</inf> stress, along with the elevated abundance of antioxidant enzyme genes, might account for the effective continuation of methanogenesis under intermittent micro-aeration conditions. This study offered a feasible method to improve the anaerobic digestion of complex substrates through the combination of P. chrysosporium supplementation and intermittent micro-aeration. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Urease-mediated homogeneous dual-mode biosensor for on-site qualitative and accurate sensitive quantitative detection of toxic soluble Aβ oligomers in undiluted samples
Abstract: In different contexts of Alzheimer's disease (AD), specific criteria for detecting toxic soluble amyloid β (Aβ) oligomers are crucial: Early detection requires highly-sensitive and accurate technology, while assessing treatment efficacy requires qualitative analysis using predefined thresholds. However, traditional methods, particularly single signal output, struggle to fulfill these criteria. Here, we present a urease-mediated homogeneous dual-mode biosensor that combines colorimetry and field-effect transistor (FET) through dual-aptamer recognition for the analysis of Aβ oligomers. This approach overcomes the challenges associated with surface modification of FET biosensors, allowing for both qualitative on-site detection (at pM levels) and highly-sensitive quantitative analysis (at fM levels) of Aβ oligomers in undiluted samples. The dual-mode biosensor displayed excellent performance in fetal bovine serum (FBS), artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF) and rabbit whole blood samples, achieving a high recovery rate ranging from 96.1 % to 101 % and a low relative standard deviation between 1.7 % and 5.1 % when detecting Aβ oligomers in undiluted samples. Furthermore, clinical tests of serum and plasma samples from AD patients and healthy individuals also verified the sensitivity and specificity of the proposed dual-mode biosensor, demonstrating its potential application in early screening and monitoring of AD treatment processes. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Highly integrated silk fibroin/nanohydroxyapatite hybrid composites via interface engineering for enhancing bone regeneration
Abstract: Composite materials incorporating natural biopolymers and inorganic minerals are attractive alternatives to mimic the physicochemical properties of native bone tissues and have been increasingly applied in the field of bone defect repair. However, the poor interfacial bonding between organic and inorganic phases in traditional composite biomaterials leads to serious organic-inorganic phase separation and inevitable agglomeration of inorganic minerals, resulting in their insufficient mechanical properties and weak bone remodeling activity. Herein, a covalent bond-mediated interface engineering strategy between silk fibroin macromolecules and hydroxyapatite nanoparticles is adopted to develop novel organic-inorganic hybrid composites (named mSF/mHA/BP) with impressively high interfacial compatibility. This method significantly enhances the interfacial bonding between organic and inorganic phases and achieves uniform distribution of inorganic nanoparticles, endowing mSF/mHA/BP with exceptional load-bearing capacity, strengthened mechanical performance, and superior anti-crack propagation. Besides ensuring robust physicochemical characteristics, the interface-engineered hybrid composite also provides a powerful platform for spatiotemporal regulation of bone healing progression. The additional loading of nanodrugs onto mSF/mHA/BP effectively induces the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells and the angiogenesis activity of vein endothelial cells, regulating the osteogenic metabolism and vascular network formation. In vivo rat cranial bone defect studies verify that the implantation of mSF/mHA/BP effectively accelerates the active bone remodeling process to promote the regeneration of mineralized bone tissues in the defect region, thus ensuring sufficient osseointegration and biomechanical support. Overall, this interface engineering strategy offers a new design insight for developing bone regenerative organic-inorganic composite biomaterials. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Vapor additive strategy enabling perfect crystallization of vacuum-evaporated photovoltaic perovskites
Abstract: Vacuum evaporation is widely regarded as a promising approach for the large-scale production of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) owing to its solvent-free nature, precise thickness control, and compatibility with manufacturing. However, vacuum-evaporated perovskites still suffer from poor crystallinity, small grain sizes, and high defect density, which result in significantly lower efficiency compared to solution-processed counterparts. Herein, we report a strategy that employs sequential evaporation of a methylammonium chloride (MACl) interlayer to tune the crystallization of perovskite films. The intercalation effect of MACl on lead diiodide (PbI<inf>2</inf>) is utilized to regulate the crystallization rate of perovskite through the formation of an intermediate phase, thereby achieving high-quality perovskite films. The impressive PCE of 20.03 % and 18.27 % were ultimately achieved for small-area (0.108 cm2) and large-area (15.52 cm2) devices, respectively. The unencapsulated device exhibits excellent stability, retaining 91 % of its initial PCE after 1000 h under ambient conditions (25 ± 5 °C and 30–40 % relative humidity). This work provides a novel crystallization modulation strategy for vacuum-evaporated perovskites, getting a breakthrough of PCE >20 % for fully vacuum-evaporated PSCs. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Photothermal and electrothermal superhydrophobic anti-icing/de-icing coating based on straw-derived sorbitol
Abstract: Severe icing poses a significant threat to power grid systems and energy equipment. A novel superhydrophobic coating with synergistic photothermal-electrothermal anti-icing/de-icing capabilities, based on sorbitol extracted from straw, was developed in this study. The surface microstructure and chemical composition of the coating were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), water contact angle (WCA) measurements, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Durability was assessed through continuous tape-stripping tests and acid–base immersion experiments. Furthermore, molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to investigate the superhydrophobic mechanism of the coating at the molecular level. The findings revealed that the coating had a microstructure featuring quasi-spherical nanopillars, achieved a WCA of 154°, and was capable of raising the surface temperature from −15 °C to 30 °C under a voltage of 0.8 V and an optical power density of 0.9 W/cm2. These results highlighted the excellent photothermal and electrothermal properties of the coating. After 12 h of acid–base immersion, the coating maintained good chemical durability. MD simulations indicate that lower diffusion coefficients and lower interfacial binding energies are conducive to enhancing the superhydrophobic properties of the coating. This study provides novel insights and significant theoretical support for the preparation of anti-icing/de-icing functional materials. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Bifunctional hyperbranched modifier enabled interlocking interfaces for ultra-strong recyclable carbon fiber/bio-epoxy composites
Abstract: The growing demand for sustainable materials presents critical challenges for conventional petroleum-based epoxy resins and their carbon fiber composites in terms of recyclability and sustainability, as well as for the enhancement of mechanical performance of emerging bio-epoxy systems to meet industrial standards. Here, we have developed a novel fabrication strategy for high-performance carbon fiber-reinforced composites (CFRC) based on bio-based epoxy resins. A bio-based thiol-terminated hyperbranched polymer (BMSPI-n), incorporating both imide and hexahydro-s-triazine structures, was employed to functionalize pristine carbon fiber fabrics while simultaneously serving as a toughener (BMIHE-n) for bio-based epoxy resins (DGEVA). The resulted BMIHE/DGEVA/BTCF<inf>12</inf> composites have demonstrated remarkable mechanical performance, including high tensile strength (869.88 MPa), flexural strength (865.94 MPa), and interlaminar shear strength (53.61 MPa), attributed to the synergistic effect of high cross-linking density, efficient stress transfer through interlocking interfaces, and multi-scale energy dissipation mechanisms of hyperbranched topology. Meanwhile, the presence of dynamic imide and hexahydro-s-triazine structures has endowed the composites with excellent degradability, facilitating the intact recycling of high-value carbon fibers. This finding has provided a promising pathway for developing high-strength, high-modulus, recyclable and sustainable bio-based epoxy resins and CFRCs. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Boosting ferroptosis-based therapy for intestinal pathogens: Co-assembled decoy nanoparticle-lipopeptide nano-spear with membrane-penetrating capacity and enzymatic resistance
Abstract: The escalating antibiotic resistance in chronic infections underscores the critical need for effective antibacterial therapies. In this study, we propose a self-assembled “nano-spear” triblock compound consisting of a pH-responsive coiled-coil peptide antibacterial block ((FHHFHHH)<inf>3</inf>), conjugated with a myristic acid hydrophobic block, and a Dab<inf>6</inf> stealth block. These blocks are co-polymerized via electrostatic complexation and hydrophobic packing. This compound self-assembles into micro-nano vesicles in an infection environment (pH 5.0) and polymerizes with Dab<inf>6</inf> to form a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) with a high density of positive charges on the vesicle surface. Notably, this highly positively charged material overcomes the sensitivity of CPPs to digestive enzymes. In proof-of-concept studies, the block copolymer CF-Dab, which exhibits potent antibacterial activity but is highly toxic, was co-assembled into CF-Dab/PLGA@RBC nanoparticles, thereby enhancing biocompatibility. Oral nanoparticle administration enables macropinocytosis-mediated cellular uptake and bacterial membrane-targeted in situ self-assembly, inducing membrane collapse. Additionally, these nanoparticles act as decoys to competitively neutralize lipid peroxides through the red blood cell membrane within the copolymer, bypassing the classical GPX4 antioxidant defense mechanism and alleviating pathogenic intestinal infections. The nano-spear strategy eliminates complex compound modifications, providing a versatile solution to toxicity and intestinal delivery barriers—major translational challenges in therapeutic development. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: High-entropy sulfide and nanozyme hybrid system with synergistic interface-engineering: Ultra-sensitive photoelectrochemical detection of chloramphenicol
Abstract: Chloramphenicol (CAP) is a broad-spectrum antibiotic commonly used for disease prevention and treatment, but its entry into human body through food chains can pose serious health risks. In this work, multi-interface high-entropy sulfide (CdMnCoZnNi)S<inf>x</inf> was synthesized by a one-pot solvothermal method, and utilized to construct a novel photoelectrochemical (PEC) aptasensor for chloramphenicol (CAP) detection. The (CdMnCoZnNi)S<inf>x</inf> exhibited excellent PEC activity, as manifested by a set of techniques. Meanwhile, a homemade PtRuFeCoMn high-entropy alloy nanozyme played a pivotal role in catalyzing 3,3′-dimethyldiphenylamine (DAB) oxidation in the presence of H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>, producing insoluble precipitates that significantly amplified the detection signals. Benefiting from these advantages, the developed PEC sensor demonstrated a wide linear detection range of 0.001–100 ng mL−1 and an ultra-low detection limit of 0.75 pg mL−1. The sensor's effectiveness was validated through successful application in analysis of real water samples, accompanied by a comprehensive health risk assessment. This study provides a simple and efficient approach for monitoring antibiotic contamination in aquatic environment and highlights significant potential of advanced high-entropy materials in biosensing and bio-catalysis. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Simultaneous exciton control and electron recycling in pyrene-based stable blue fluorescent organic light-emitting diodes via hybridized local and charge transfer and triplet-triplet fusion mechanisms
Abstract: While anthracene-based fluorescent materials utilizing triplet–triplet fusion (TTF) can theoretically achieve internal quantum efficiencies (IQEs) up to 62.5 %, their performance is hindered by non-emissive high-lying triplet state (T<inf>n</inf>, n ≥ 2) excitons and instability caused by electron leakage. To address this, we report a pyrene-based fluorescent emitter, 9-(4-(6-(4-(1-phenyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)phenyl)pyren-1-yl)phenyl)-9H-carbazole (p-CPI), which simultaneously exhibits TTF and hybridized local and charge transfer (HLCT) characteristics. Transient electroluminescence (TrEL) and magneto-electroluminescence (MEL) measurements confirm that the HLCT pathway facilitates high-lying reverse intersystem crossing (hRISC), allowing non-radiative triplet excitons to contribute to emission, thereby suppressing triplet-related quenching and enhancing device stability. As a result, a non-doped p-CPI device achieves an LT<inf>70</inf> (the time taken for the luminance to decrease to 70 % of its initial value) of 115 h, corresponding to more than a 50-fold improvement in operational lifetime compared to a conventional TTF-based device. Furthermore, when used as an electron harnessing and recycling (EHR) layer between the emissive layer (EML) and electron blocking layer (EBL), p-CPI captures and recycles leakage electrons while protecting the EBL from degradation, resulting in a slightly improved external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 7.49 % and extending the operational lifetime to an LT<inf>70</inf> of 27 h, more than a twofold enhancement compared to the reference device. This dual-channel exciton management and EHR strategy offers a promising approach for overcoming the long-standing efficiency-lifetime trade-off in blue fluorescent organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: In-situ photocatalysis enabled preparation of high-performance flexible inductive electrodes in triboelectric nanogenerators
Abstract: The induction electrode plays a critical role in determining triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) performance through electrostatic induction. However, traditional fabrication methods involving metal tape adhesion face inherent limitations: i. The adhesive layer increases induction distance (which is inversely proportional to maximum surface charge density), consequently reducing output; ii. Their susceptibility to inelastic deformation prevents reliable operation under flexible/elastic strain required by wearable devices. To address these challenges, we developed a novel in-situ photocatalytic method for synthesizing silver nanoparticle (AgNPs) electrodes. Achievable even with ambient sunlight, this simple synthesis process can be accelerated to 1 min using high-power illumination. This method eliminates the adhesive layer required by traditional electrodes, enabling exceptional flexibility, stability, and adaptability. Free from expensive instruments, our low-cost method achieves 187 % enhanced output over traditional electrodes, rivaling magnetron-sputtered electrodes. The AgNPs electrode hybridized with minimal silver nanowires (AgNWs) exhibits superior resistance stability compared to the pure AgNWs electrode, using only 2.5 % AgNWs nano-material. Benefiting from the structural merits of AgNPs and their hybrid architecture, the developed electrodes achieve good flexibility and elastic strain performance. These advancements demonstrate the high potential of AgNPs induction electrodes for high-performance TENGs and wearable applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: High-performance triboelectric nanogenerator based on mangosteen peel-derived carbon for energy harvesting and self-powered sensing
Abstract: This study presents the successful development of a novel, sustainable, and carbon-based triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) utilizing biomass waste. Through a simple carbonization and activation process, mangosteen peel-derived carbon materials (MPC) with abundant pore structures were obtained. The resulting MPC was employed as the electrode in the TENG. The fabricated MPC-based TENG (MPC-TENG) harvested mechanical energy from both the human body and surrounding environment, converting it into electrical energy or signals. The optimized MPC-TENG device exhibits remarkable electrical output, effective human motion detection, and excellent mechanical durability. It generated an open-circuit voltage of 758 V, short-circuit current of 10.08 μA (at 7 Hz), and power density of 909 mW/m2. Furthermore, the device powered up to 671 commercially available blue and white LEDs connected in series. The MPC-TENG sensor successfully facilitated human gesture (e.g., fist wheel/finger/palm tapping) and gait recognition, exhibiting excellent water resistance and minimal signal fluctuation after 14,000 cycles. These exceptional performance characteristics are attributed to the activation-induced high specific surface area (952 m2/g), abundant pore architecture (0.41 cm3/g), enhanced defect density (I<inf>D</inf>/I<inf>G</inf> ratio: 1.03 → 1.07), higher N self-doping content (1.2 → 1.6 at.%), and improved dielectric constant (3.0 → 4.3 at 1 kHz). This study offers a novel perspective on the development of biomass-based TENGs with extended lifetimes and enhanced output performance. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Electro-microbial destruction of ‘forever chemicals’: Recent advances and imminent challenges
Abstract: The widespread presence of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), or “forever chemicals,” poses significant environmental and public health challenges due to their persistence and toxic effects. Characterized by strong carbon‑fluorine (C[sbnd]F) bonds, PFAS resist natural degradation, leading to contamination of soil, water, and organisms. These synthetic compounds originate from various sources, such as industrial discharges, firefighting foams, and consumer products, with exposure routes including contaminated drinking water, food, and air. Risks associated with PFAS exposure include endocrine disruption, developmental disorders, immunotoxicity, and cancer, highlighting the urgent need for effective destruction technologies. This review evaluates advanced destruction methods for PFAS, focusing on microbial biotransformation, electrochemical degradation, and bioelectrochemical systems (BES). Microbial approaches utilize microorganisms to break down PFAS under anaerobic conditions, while electrochemical methods cleave carbon‑fluorine bonds through reactive species. BES combines microbial and electrochemical reactions for enhanced efficiency. Despite advancements, challenges remain, including incomplete defluorination, toxic intermediates, high costs, and scalability issues. This review addresses the mechanisms, advantages, and limitations of each technique, underscoring the need for interdisciplinary approaches to develop sustainable solutions. The findings aim to guide researchers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders in mitigating the impacts of forever chemicals on health and the environment. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Selective catalytic activation of peroxymonocarbonate over a Co[sbnd]Cu co-embedded alginate hydrogel spheres for efficient antibiotic degradation
Abstract: Activated permonocarbonate (PMC) systems hold significant promise for the removal of aquaculture antibiotics from complex water matrices but are constrained by the lack of highly selective activation techniques. To address this, Co(II) and Cu(II) co-embedded alginate hydrogel spheres (Co/Cu@AHS) were developed as a heterogeneous activator, and their efficacy in selectively activating PMC was evaluated using ciprofloxacin (CIP) as a model antibiotic pollutant. The activation performance was investigated under various hydrogel synthesis conditions, operational parameters and water matrices. Notably, under optimal conditions (10 mM NaHCO<inf>3</inf> and 5 mM H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>), a CIP removal efficiency of 99.4 % was achieved within 30 min, accompanied by a reaction rate constant of 0.1685 min−1 and an oxidant utilization efficiency of 97.2 %. This was attributed to the selective activation of PMC by Co/Cu@AHS, which generated a large number of radical and non-radical reactive species (e.g. ·OH, CO<inf>3</inf>·−, 1O<inf>2</inf>, ·O<inf>2</inf>−, Co(IV) and Cu(III)). Mechanistic studies elucidated the synergistic redox interactions between Co and Cu in detail, revealing an electron donor-acceptor mechanism that enables more efficient PMC activation compared to single-metal system. Degradation pathway analysis, based on LC-MS and density functional theory calculations, indicated that defluorination, decarboxylation, and piperazine epoxidation were the main degradation routes for CIP transformation. Toxicity assessment further demonstrated a reduction in the toxicity of the degradation intermediates. The hydrogel spheres also exhibited minimal metal leaching (<1.0 mg/L), excellent reusability over eight cycles, and robustness in real water quality matrices. Moreover, the feasibility of in-situ generation of PMC using CO<inf>2</inf> for antibiotic control was explored. This study presents a sustainable and high-performance strategy for highly selective activation of PMC and the control of antibiotics in aquaculture effluents. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Current advances in furfural reduction to furfuryl alcohol via thermal- and electrocatalysis
Abstract: Reproducible organic carbon sources with inherent sustainability, biology based compounds possess potential to serve as prime feedstocks for conversion into premium-grade chemical derivatives and alternative bio-fuels, presenting an environmentally conscious solution to energy security issues arising from depleting petroleum resources. Furfuryl alcohol (FFA), a versatile bio-based platform chemical with wide industrial applications, is predominantly produced via the catalytic hydrogenation of furfural (FFR), a key renewable intermediate derived from lignocellulosic biomass. This state-of-the-art review decodes breakthrough strategies in FFR valorization, particularly focusing on emerging FFA production pathways through advanced catalytic systems, systematically categorizing the transformation routes into three reaction pathways: conventional hydrogenation process, catalytic transfer hydrogenation and electrochemical hydrogenation. Furthermore, we highlight the latest advancements in innovative catalytic material design, aiming to offer strategic guidance for achieving highly FFA production via specific reaction pathways. Finally, the technical challenges and future research directions associated with the three FFR-to-FFA conversion routes are critically analyzed so that it could denote an obvious methodology for designing innovative catalysts. This review is anticipated to establish a comprehensive guidance for designing efficient and selective catalysts, ultimately advancing the scalable industrial implementation of biomass valorization. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Sonodynamic nanocatalytic therapy: ultrasound-activated PVA/nanocellulose-tannic acid hydrogels for mechano-antimicrobial plaque disruption and enamel-safe chromophore degradation
Abstract: Periodontitis represents a chronic inflammatory disorder triggered by multi-species oral bacterial infection of periodontal tissues. If left untreated, this condition can culminate in severe consequences, including alveolar bone resorption and loss of tooth support architecture. Given these clinical challenges, the development of a safe and effective strategy for plaque elimination and dental whitening remains a critical unmet need in periodontal care. To address this, we report the design and fabrication of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-based hydrogel loaded with tannic acid @ nanocellulose nanoparticles (PTAN). This novel composite system demonstrates dual functionality: robust antibacterial activity and biocompatible teeth-whitening efficacy. Under ultrasonic irradiation, the cavitation-generated mechanical forces drive targeted attachment of tannic acid @ nanocellulose nanoparticles (TAN) to bacterial surfaces. This process induces bidirectional impact and frictional forces, rendering bacterial cell walls mechanically sensitive. Additionally, it promotes the production of hydroxyl radicals and singlet oxygen, while enhancing the transmission of tannic acid-mediated death signals to pathogens. Concurrently, the hydrogel's porous architecture synergizes with the polyphenolic binding capacity of tannic acid to pigmented substrates. This dual-mechanism enables efficient capture and adsorption of chromogenic molecules within the hydrogel matrix. Collectively, our findings establish PTAN hydrogel as a rapid, highly effective, and biocompatible strategy for simultaneous plaque removal and dental decolorization, offering promising translational potential for clinical periodontal therapy. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Preparation of ordered polyaniline by interfacial polymerization and application in Zn2+ hybrid supercapacitor
Abstract: As one of the most common cathode materials for Zn2+ hybrid supercapacitor (ZHSC), polyaniline (PANI) is still facing problems such as low practical capacity and poor long-term cycling stability. In this study, we prepared the ordered polyaniline (PANI-i) with high crystallinity by the optimized interfacial polymerization as a promising cathode material for ZHSC. It was found that PANI-i had a vertically aligned nanofiber network structure with a diameter of 150–250 nm, high crystallinity and tight π-π stacking conducive to the enhanced ion transport efficiency and structural stability. Just as expected, the specific capacitance of PANI-i reaches as higher as 496.5 F g−1 at 10 mV s−1, which is 4.6 times higher than that of traditional solution polymerization polyaniline (PANI-s); and its charge transfer resistance (0.66 Ω) and diffusion resistance (σ = 0.18 Ω s-1/2) are significantly lower than PANI-s. Notably, ZHSC assembled with PANI-i provides an ultra-high specific energy of 143.7 Wh kg−1 at 996.9 W kg−1, which outperforms most of the reported materials. Due to the higher crystallinity and structural stability of PANI-i, ZHSC achieves 97.2 % capacity retention after 5000 cycles even at 1 A g−1. Kinetic analysis confirmed the synergistic domination by surface pseudocapacitance and diffusion processes for the charge storage of PANI-i and the effectively optimized Zn2+ adsorption/diffusion pathways by the nanofiber network structure. This study provides a new strategy for the upgrading performance of traditional conductive polyaniline and demonstrates the more in-depth applications of interfacial polymerization technology in high-performance electrode materials for energy storage devices. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Partial oxidation doped strategy for high performance and stable perovskite solar cells
Abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) face efficiency and stability limitations from electron transport layer (ETL) defects and carrier interfacial recombination. In this manuscript, a partial hydrolysis oxidation doping strategy is designed by introducing ammonium persulfate (APS) into SnO<inf>2</inf> ETL to simultaneously enhances device performance and stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reactive species (HSO<inf>4</inf>−, H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>, and NH<inf>4</inf>+) generated during APS hydrolysis act synergistically: effectively passivating oxygen vacancies (V<inf>O</inf>) and Sn2+ defects on SnO<inf>2</inf> surface, thereby optimizing its band structure and electron mobility; and significantly reducing Pb2+ and I− vacancy defects in the perovskite phase via coordination interaction, leading to improved crystallization kinetics. The optimized devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.32 % with negligible hysteresis and retain 95.3 % initial efficiency after 1500 h ambient storage. This dual-passivation approach provides new insights for developing stable and high-efficiency PSCs. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Metal-organic molecules for aqueous Zn[sbnd]I2 batteries: synergistic redox acceleration and shuttle effect inhibition
Abstract: Aqueous zinc‑iodine (Zn[sbnd]I<inf>2</inf>) batteries are considered promising energy storage systems due to their high energy density, improved safety, and low cost. However, their advanced performances are severely limited by the sluggish redox kinetics of iodine and the polyiodide shuttling effect, which leads to irreversible loss of active material and zinc anode corrosion, thereby degrading cycling stability and overall performance. In this work, copper acetylacetonate (Cu(acac)<inf>2</inf>) is employed as a metal-organic molecular catalyst to construct high-performance and long-lasting Zn[sbnd]I<inf>2</inf> batteries. Material characterizations and density functional theory calculations reveal that Cu(acac)<inf>2</inf> exhibits dual functionalities: (1) chemically adsorbing iodide/polyiodide species to suppress the shuttling effect, and (2) catalyzing iodine redox reactions to enhance reaction kinetics. The Zn-I₂ batteries assembled with Cu(acac)<inf>2</inf> as the cathode material can achieve an extraordinary cycling lifespan of over 55,000 cycles at 4 A g−1 with a minimal capacity decay rate of 0.00086 % per cycle, along with an average coulombic efficiency of 99.86 %, surpassing the performance of carbon-based cathodes. In-situ Raman spectroscopy further demonstrates that Zn[sbnd]I<inf>2</inf> batteries using Cu(acac)<inf>2</inf> cathodes maintain significantly lower polyiodide concentrations during charge/discharge processes compared to those using active carbon cathodes, confirming its dual role in suppressing shuttling and catalyzing reactions. This work highlights the effectiveness of molecular catalysts in mitigating polyiodide shuttling and offers a novel approach to developing high-performance aqueous Zn[sbnd]I<inf>2</inf> batteries. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Versatile, cost-effective and highly-multiplex nucleic acid detection through the Engineered Hairpin Cleavage Amplification (EHCA) strategy
Abstract: Real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR), droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), and CRISPR/Cas diagnostics typically rely on expensive, target-specific fluorescence probes or CRISPR RNA (crRNA) for precise nucleic acid detection, and their multiplexing capability is limited by the scarcity of fluorescent colors in fluorometric thermal cyclers. To overcome these limitations, we introduced Engineered Hairpin Cleavage Amplification (EHCA), a novel technique that is compatible with various platforms such as qPCR, ddPCR, CRISPR/Cas12a and melting curve analysis (MCA), utilizing universal fluorescence probes/crRNA. EHCA employs a unique mechanism in which Taq polymerase cleaves engineered hairpins to release secondary primers, thereby extending helper targets or fluorescence probes. EHCA, efficiently developed with the aid of computational tools, exhibited comparable detection sensitivity and precision to specific probe assays. Furthermore, EHCA-MCA demonstrated multiplexed detection capabilities by generating fluorescent double strands of different lengths (T<inf>m</inf>) and colors. Detection of nucleic acids with high sensitivity was achieved using EHCA-MCA at annealing temperatures between 46 and 66 °C, highlighting the remarkable temperature-robustness. In evaluating 213 clinical samples for high-risk HPV genotyping, the 14-plex EHCA-MCA yielded a sensitivity of 92.2 %, specificity of 98.1 % and detection accuracy of 96.7 %. With its versatility, cost-effectiveness, simplicity, high sensitivity, and multiplexing capabilities, the EHCA strategy is anticipated to be widely utilized. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Unraveling metabolic preferences and syntrophy in anaerobic methanogenesis under meso-thermophilic conditions through omics and flux balance analysis
Abstract: Biological methanation for carbon sequestration is an emerging green technology for renewable energy production within the circular economy, with anaerobic digestion (AD) playing a central role in biogas production and waste-to-power conversion. While significant research has been conducted on microbial communities in AD under thermophilic (≥ 55 °C) and mesophilic (≤ 40 °C) conditions, the mechanisms underlying efficient methanogenesis, including metabolic preferences and interspecies interactions under meso-thermophilic (41–50 °C) conditions, remain poorly understood. This study explores the microbial species involved in cellulose hydrolysis and methanogenesis under meso-thermophilic and mesophilic conditions, focusing on microbial community structure, digestate parameters, and metabolic interactions. The core microbial community consisted of 41 species, contributing over 55 % of the total abundance, and was assembled from metagenomes with high completeness and low contamination. Metabolic analysis identified Methanobacterium sp. GSMM9893 and Methanosarcina flavescens GSMM9656 as key contributors to methanogenesis under meso-thermophilic and mesophilic conditions, respectively. Five metagenome-assembled species were identified as cellulose hydrolyzers in both temperature conditions. Transcriptomic data revealed a preference for hydrogenotrophic, methylotrophic, and syntrophic acetate-oxidizing pathways for methanogenesis under meso-thermophilic conditions. Genome-scale metabolic models simulated methanogenesis, identifying the optimal synthetic methanogenic communities, MHT13 and MT8, under meso-thermophilic and mesophilic conditions, respectively. Key syntrophic acetate-oxidizing bacteria in MHT13 under meso-thermophilic conditions included six species, while MT8 under mesophilic conditions was dominated by a distinct set of six species. Flux balance simulations revealed a dynamic interaction network driven by H<inf>2</inf> and CO<inf>2</inf> uptake and acetate exchange. These findings provide new insights into the metabolic pathways for methanogenesis in meso-thermophilic anaerobic digesters and contribute to optimizing AD processes by highlighting species interactions and metabolic preferences. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Sustainable treatment of dairy industry wastewater using an integrated anaerobic membrane bioreactor-reverse osmosis system for industrial water reuse
Abstract: The increasing demand for water in industrial processes has prompted the exploration of sustainable water management technologies. This study investigated the integration of an anaerobic membrane bioreactor (AnMBR) with reverse osmosis (RO) for energy recovery and water reuse in the dairy industry. The AnMBR system, fed with dairy industry wastewater, was operated under mesophilic conditions, and its treatment and filtration performances were evaluated. The permeate from the AnMBR system was subsequently treated by the RO system, and the quality of reclaimed water was assessed for potential industrial reuse. The methane yield from anaerobic digestion of dairy industry wastewater was 0.214 ± 0.008 mL CH<inf>4</inf>/g COD<inf>fed</inf>. The RO permeate quality met EPA standards, and the combined AnMBR + RO system operated at a cost of 0.46 €/m3. The findings of this study demonstrated that the AnMBR + RO system could produce treated water suitable for use as makeup water in cooling towers, offering a sustainable alternative for industrial water reuse and reducing the overall water footprint. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Anti-icing and fast deicing of superhydrophobic elastic film with electrothermal heating and pneumatic inflation
Abstract: Superhydrophobic surface exhibits a considerable anti−/deicing capacity due to its low ice adhesion strength. However, in many cases, the ice easily penetrates the rough structures of superhydrophobic surface to form a mechanical interlocking between the ice and solid surface, conversely resulting in an extremely high ice adhesion strength and loss of the anti−/deicing capacity. Here, we develop a superhydrophobic elastic film (SEF) with the functions of electrothermal heating and pneumatic inflation at the same time, which significantly alleviate the deicing obstacle caused by the mechanical interlocking of the ice. Furthermore, the SEF has a thickness of only 201 μm while demonstrates the excellent chemical and mechanical durability with the contact angle higher than 152° and sliding angle lower than 10° after being stretching to 1152 % or 1500 cycles at 500 % strain. Benefiting from the excellent deformation/recovery capability of the SEF, an efficient deicing by pneumatic inflation can be achieved. Even in the extremely cold conditions, deicing also can be achieved by the electrothermal assisted pneumatic inflation. Such design provides a lightweight, low-consumption and high-efficiency solution in the field of anti-icing through the synergistic innovation of material-structure-control, which may be a key research direction for the next-generation intelligent anti-icing system. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Enhanced magnetic harvest of microalgae cultivated in municipal wastewater using polymeric aluminum chloride nano-Fe3O4 with cost-effective nanoparticles recovery
Abstract: Nano-Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf> coated with polymeric aluminum chloride (Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC) was used as magnetic flocculants to harvest Scenedesmus obliquus cultivated in municipal wastewater. The impact of Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC dosage, pH value, and stirring rate on harvesting efficiency was investigated. The effect of combining magnetic nanomaterials recovery with lipid extraction was evaluated, and its influence on biodiesel recovery was analyzed. Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC composite exhibited a reduced saturation magnetization of 73.53 emu/g compared to 92.32 emu/g for nano-Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>. Zeta potential revealed a positive charge on Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC (45.6 mV), which could facilitate the harvest of negatively charged S. obliquus cells. Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC successfully achieved a harvesting efficiency of 98.6 % in lab-scale at short harvest time of 90 s, dosage of 55.36 mg/L, pH of 6.3, and stirring speed of 396 rpm. Outdoor harvest showed a harvesting efficiency up to 94.3 % in 180 s. Lipid and fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs) content after Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC harvest (26.4 and 19.5 % of dw, respectively) showed insignificant differences with those obtained via centrifugation. Interestingly, this method showed 82 % magnetic nano-Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf> recovery after lipid extraction and did not affect the quality of the produced biodiesel. An economic analysis based on chemical inputs revealed that Fe<inf>3</inf>O<inf>4</inf>@PAC is cost-effective for biomass harvest ($2 per kg biomass) compared to other magnetic flocculants, offering potential for large-scale applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Nano-lanthanum oxide and polyvinylpyrrolidone additives enhance PVDF-based polymer electrolytes to enable safe and durable design of lithium metal batteries
Abstract: Polymer electrolytes (PEs) are essential for high-energy-density, safe, and durable lithium metal batteries (LMBs). However, their widespread adoption is hindered by inherent challenges such as low ionic conductivity and uneven lithium deposition. Here, we present an innovative strategy to engineer a novel polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based polymer electrolyte by incorporating lithium-ion nonconductive fillers and polymer additives. The optimized electrolyte exhibits remarkable ionic conductivity (≈0.31 mS·cm−1) and mechanical toughness (≈ 393 %), attributed to the synergistic interaction between lanthanum oxide (La<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf>) and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP). Specifically, oxygen vacancies in La<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> strongly adsorb bis(trifluoromethane sulfonyl)imide anions (TFSI−), promoting free lithium-ion mobility, while the C[dbnd]O groups in PVP engage in ion-dipole interactions with lithium ions, ensuring uniform ion flux. This dual mechanism facilitates rapid and stable lithium-ion transport, resulting in an expanded electrochemical stability window (4.61 V) and an elevated lithium-ion transfer number (t<inf>Li</inf>+ = 0.54). In practical applications, LMBs employing this electrolyte demonstrated exceptional cycling stability, achieving 200 cycles with a capacity retention of 75.3 % at 1.5C. This work presents a novel strategy for the construction of high-performance polymer electrolytes and establishes a basis for next-generation LMBs with improved safety and efficiency. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Tailoring polyester crosslinking networks for multifunctional wood composites
Abstract: Wood is a natural biomaterial and plays an important role in global carbon neutralization. To optimize its application, wood modification is needed to overcome drawbacks in dimensional stability, absolute strength, and microbial resistance. The in-situ polyesterification of citric acid and sorbitol (SorCA) in wood is a green and effective method to improve its properties; however, different polyester crosslinking networks have significant and complex effects. By adjusting the monomer ratio, the polyester structure varies from linear to highly crosslinked, altering multiscale interactions with wood components. High crosslinking density polyesters form in cellulose amorphous regions, where chemical bonds and intermolecular forces induce a more ordered cellulose chain arrangement. This enhances water resistance, with mechanical performance improvements including a 138.6 % increase in modulus of elasticity, a 14.7 % increase in modulus of rupture, and a 110.7 % increase in compressive strength, expanding the potential for structural applications. In contrast, linear polyesters enable ether bonding with lignin, forming compact networks via lignin-carbohydrate complex (LCC) interactions. This suppresses wood's dimensional changes in humid conditions, offering ideal moisture stability. Moreover, the linear flexible network alleviates the toughness loss caused by rigid polyesters. The synergy between cellulose structural optimization and polyester crosslinking network reinforcement reconstructs wood's nanoscale ultrastructure, enabling performance-tailored composites. By unveiling the “structure–property” response mechanism of wood polyesterification, this study proposes new strategies for high-performance, sustainable wood composite development. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: In situ anchored nano zero-valent copper on ellagic acid-derived covalent organic frameworks: a dual-function strategy for antifouling and uranium enrichment from seawater
Abstract: Uranium extraction from seawater is regarded as an efficient approach to address the fuel supply issue in the development of nuclear energy. Herein, the covalent organic framework (EPCu-COF) was synthesized with the copper perfluorophthalocyanine and ellagic acid as construction units, and subsequent alkaline treatment and reduction reactions successfully led to the development of the dual-functional COFs (R-EPCu-COF-TA) for uranium extraction. Compared with EPCu-COF, the -COOH and -OH groups in the dual-functional COFs enhanced their hydrophilicity and selectivity, and the anchored Cu(0) not only reduced U(VI) but also exhibited effective antibacterial capabilities. The batch experiments found that R-EPCu-COF-TA exhibited a remarkable extraction capacity of 588.3 mg/g in the uranium-spiked seawater. Meanwhile, when subject to a 30 days extraction from natural seawater, the material's adsorption capacity for U(VI) reached 2.92 mg/g. More importantly, research into antibacterial properties showed that the R-EPCu-COF-TA had anti-bioadhesion capabilities, which could effectively inhibit bacterial growth. Mechanistic analysis demonstrated that U(VI) was initially coordinated by -COOH and -OH groups, then Cu(0) further reduced it to low-valence uranium. Thus, this COF holds extensive application prospects in the domain of uranium extraction from seawater. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dual-functionalized wearable SERS substrates enable ultra-sensitive detection of lung cancer biomarkers in sweat
Abstract: The non-invasive detection of lung cancer is promising but remains challenging owing to the low biomarker concentrations in biofluids. To address this, we present a wearable biosensing platform that integrates a silver nanowire-hydrogel composite surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) hotspots and an AI algorithm to enable non-invasive lung cancer screening through sweat analysis. The platform features three synergistic innovations: (1) a conformal AgNW-hydrogel composite structure generating 3D plasmonic hotspots, achieving ultrahigh sensitivity (0.1 pM detection limit for aldehyde biomarkers); (2) dual-functionalized substrates (4-ATP/4-MPBA) for selective enrichment of glycoproteins and oxidative stress markers directly from epidermal sweat; (3) A CNN-based spectral classifier (AlexNet) decoding metabolic fingerprints with 99 % diagnostic accuracy. This integrated approach bridges nanomaterial engineering, molecular diagnostics, and artificial intelligence and offers a transformative strategy for point-of-care cancer screening. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Process Intensification of the Fischer-Tropsch synthesis using conductive packed POCS with skin: the role of the POCS design parameters
Abstract: Heat management poses severe challenges when dealing with highly exothermic and endothermic reactions. In this paper we study the design of structured packed beds with highly conductive (Al) cellular internals during the Fischer-Tropsch (FT) synthesis in a tubular reactor with external cooling. A structured packed bed consists of an interconnected matrix with a well-defined geometry packed with catalyst particles. Herein we focus on 3D printed Periodic Open Cellular Structures (POCS), which allow a fully tailored design of their geometry. Moreover, the 3D printing technique enables introduction of elements in addition to just the cellular structure and adoption of different materials for manufacturing. An external skin on the outer diameter of the POCS lattice has been printed, starting from the same aluminum alloy powder, to form the so called POCS with skin. This choice was made to improve the contact with the reactor walls, which is considered one of the major heat transfer resistances. The POCS have been tested in the Fischer-Tropsch synthesis, a highly exothermic and temperature sensitive reaction, which makes heat management pivotal. The tests on POCS with skin have been performed in a semi pilot-scale rig equipped to fully qualify the heat transfer performances of the structured reactor. 3D printed elements have been tested to explore the effects of the following POCS features: porosities or relative density (RD<inf>lattice</inf>), specific surface area (S<inf>v</inf>), and Gap between the external diameter of the POCS and the reactor walls. The results show the dominant effect of the relative density of the element when compared to the other parameters. Furthermore, it appears that a threshold value exists below which the structured catalytic bed is unaffected by the initial Gap, which from our experimental conditions is about 40–50 μm. This study paves the way for the optimization of those structures in terms of internal design and contact with the wall, aiming at improving the overall heat transfer coefficient, maximizing productivity and reducing the manufacturing efforts. During our tests, we were able to pack about 3.75 g/cm of catalyst in a 20 cm long, 1-inch I.D., single tube reactor, estimating an overall heat transfer coefficient larger than 1200 W/m2/K and enabling the removal of 1.2 MW/m3. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Efficient degradation and deiodination of iopamidol by synergistic •OH and SO4•− oxidation in O3/PMS system
Abstract: Iodinated X-ray contrast media (ICM) are a major source of organic iodine in wastewaters. Current wastewater treatment processes are not effective in eliminating ICM. This study investigates the degradation of ICM in O<inf>3</inf>/peroxymonosulfate (PMS)system, which simultaneously generates hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and sulfate radicals (SO<inf>4</inf>•−). Both radicals exhibit high reactivity toward an ICM surrogate, iopamidol (k<inf>·OH,iopmidol</inf>= (2.58 ± 0.15) × 109 M−1 s−1 and k<inf>SO<inf>4</inf>·−,iopmidol</inf> = (5.18 ± 0.26) × 109 M−1 s−1), thereby exhibiting a synergistic elimination effect. We also systematically evaluate the influence of other factors (including PMS concentration, pH, bicarbonate, and chloride) in affecting the degradation kinetics. Notably, SO<inf>4</inf>•− suggest a higher deiodination efficiency (87.2 %) than that of •OH. Complete oxidation of inorganic iodine to iodate was achieved in the O<inf>3</inf>/PMS, whereas residual iodide was still detected in O<inf>3</inf>/H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>, likely due to the reduction of HOI/OI− by H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>. Theoretical Fukui index calculations, in combination with UPLC-TOF-MS/MS analysis, were employed to identify the reactive sites on IPM and elucidate its transformation pathway under radical attacks. •OH primarily degrades iopamidol via combination pathways of the cleavage of the side chain and the oxidation of alkane. In contrast, SO<inf>4</inf>•− favors the deiodination to form corresponding hydroxylation products, thereby oxidizing amino group to generate nitro congeners. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that O<inf>3</inf>/PMS effectively degrades iopamidol and transfer organic iodine to nontoxic iodate, which holds potential in minimizing the formation of iodo-disinfection byproducts in real-world applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Valence-state engineering of Cu species on TiO2 surfaces for synergistic enhancement of photocatalytic CO2 reduction activity and products selectivity
Abstract: Copper serves as an exceptional cocatalyst, enhancing CO<inf>2</inf> molecular adsorption-activation and stabilizing reaction intermediates, thus demonstrating remarkable potential in photocatalytic CO<inf>2</inf> conversion to diverse hydrocarbons. However, the complex and variable oxidation states of Cu make the role and mechanism of low-valent Cu species (Cu0/Cu+) in CO<inf>2</inf> photoreduction poorly understood. This study precisely controlled the valence distribution of Cu species on TiO<inf>2</inf> surfaces using a red phosphorus-mediated hydrothermal synthesis strategy, successfully constructing an efficient catalyst for CO<inf>2</inf> photoreduction. The optimized composite exhibits a CH<inf>4</inf> evolution rate of 64.44 μmol·g−1·h−1 under simulated sunlight, representing a 54-fold improvement over pristine TiO<inf>2</inf> while maintaining high selectivity of 86 %. The enhanced photocatalytic performance and product selectivity originate from Cu incorporation, which substantially improves light absorption capacity, prolongs charge carrier lifetime, and reduces charge transfer resistance. Combined characterization and DFT calculations conclusively demonstrate that Cu0 and Cu+ serve as the active sites for CH<inf>4</inf> and CO generation, respectively. The key intermediate *CO preferentially desorbs as CO from Cu+ sites, while *CO adsorbed on Cu0 sites undergoes further hydrogenation to form CH<inf>4</inf>. This work provides novel strategies for developing efficient CO<inf>2</inf> photoreduction catalysts and elucidates the atomic-scale mechanistic role of Cu valence states in regulating CO<inf>2</inf> reduction pathways. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
