Title: Co-regulated proton confinement and uptake mechanisms for ultra-fast and robust aqueous Zn-organic batteries
Abstract: Central to the progression of aqueous zinc-organic batteries (AZOBs) is the exploration of durable organic hosts capable of fast ion diffusion within electrolytes and electrode interiors. Compared with Zn2+ insertion, developing proton-storage organic cathodes along with optimizing charge transport across the cathode-electrolyte interface remains difficult but critical for improved AZOBs. Herein, quinone-based molecules, particularly Menadione (2-methyl,1–4, naphthoquinone), were uniformly separated onto negative-charged porous carbon (PC) particles as the organic cathode. Due to the negative-charged −COOH and − OH groups, H+ movement is confined merely inside the cathode to eliminating interfacial charge transport barriers for fast-charging and robust PC-supported Menadione cathode based on reversible C=O/C-OH reaction. As a result, Zn//Menadione battery exhibits an ultra-high capacity (313 mAh g−1), superb rate capability, and ultra-long lifespan over 20,000 cycles at 30 A g−1, superior to most reported organic cathodes. This work provides novel insights into exploring proton-insertion chemistry within small organic cathodes for advanced Zn batteries. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dual-strategy anti-fouling based on hydrogel-coated catalytic separation membrane material
Abstract: Membrane fouling is one of the key problems limiting the application of membrane separation technology. To address the fouling of membranes in complex oily wastewater, this study developed a dual strategy that employs a superhydrophilic fiber membrane with catalytic capabilities to mitigate the various types of fouling on the membranes. First, ZIF 67 was loaded onto fibers by in situ growth. Then, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitosan (CS) were cross-linked to form a dual-network hydrogel with which the catalyst-loaded fibrous membranes were wrapped to obtain the target product, H-ZP/NW. H-ZP/NW with catalyst loading and H-P/NW without catalyst loading have excellent superhydrophilic and underwater superoleophobicity, and the oil-water separation efficiencies remain above 97 % for different oil-water mixtures. In addition, the fiber membranes have excellent adsorption ability for dyes, especially anionic dyes. H-ZP/NW has stable catalytic ability in both Flow-through mode (FT) and liquid-phase batch (LB) mode. The removal rate of Methylene Blue (MB) is above 95 %, and surprisingly, the removal rate of MB by H-P/NW in FT mode is also up to 75 % or more, and the reaction has a hysteresis. The separation effect of fiber membranes on complex oil-water emulsions containing MB proved the ability of fiber membranes to resist various contaminants and their potential application in the purification of oily wastewater. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Vacuum pressure swing adsorption for continuous xenon removal and helium recovery in molten salt reactor off-gas treatment
Abstract: Xenon (Xe), a noble gas generated as a fission product in molten salt reactors (MSRs), poses operational and environmental challenges due to its radiological nature and its detrimental impact on neutron economy. To address these issues, we evaluated the feasibility of a vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) system employing microporous activated carbon for selective separation of Xe from simulated MSR off-gas streams. The physical and thermal properties of the adsorbent were systematically characterized, and both equilibrium and dynamic Xe adsorption behaviors were investigated under varying conditions. The effects of adsorption pressure, desorption pressure, and cycle duration on separation performance were analyzed in detail. Under optimized conditions, the VPSA process achieved Xe removal and helium (He) recovery efficiencies exceeding 99 % and 95 %, respectively. While previous studies have focused on recovering non-radioactive Xe from ambient air or industrial sources, its application to radiologically sensitive MSR off-gas systems remains insufficiently studied. The proposed process demonstrated effective He reuse and operational robustness, indicating its potential as a regenerable and energy-efficient gas purification method. These findings are expected to support the development of safe and sustainable off-gas management strategies for next-generation nuclear systems and offer valuable insights into selective noble gas separation for environmental and industrial applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Role of lignite and derived semicoke in nitrogen fixation during co-pyrolysis of protein-rich biomass: Physical or chemical adsorbent?
Abstract: For preparation of nitrogen-doped materials and elimination of NO<inf>x</inf> precursors, there have been increased efforts to enhance nitrogen fixation in pyrolysis. Lignite and derived semicoke have been widely used in adsorption of NH<inf>3</inf>. In this work, spent coffee grounds (SCG), Xiaolongtan (XLT) lignite and its derived semicoke (XLT600) were selected as nitrogen source and adsorbents in pyrolysis, in order to clarify specific action sites on adsorbents and corresponding mechanism in NH<inf>3</inf>-semicoke interactions. Layered pyrolysis, thermogravimetric infrared spectroscopy and temperature-programmed desorption (TPD) method were combined for decoupling of NH<inf>3</inf> release and retention in pyrolysis. Noncovalent interactions analyses and transition state theory were combined to further verify physical and chemical adsorption of NH<inf>3</inf> onto various functional groups. The results showed that presence of XLT600 suppressed release of NH<inf>3</inf> in range of 250–400 °C. Similarly, less nitrogen (22.53 %) was captured by cellulose when urea was blended with XLT600, compared to that (26.48 %) impacted by XLT. Phenolic –OH and COOH could form stronger hydrogen bonds with NH<inf>3</inf> than C[dbnd]O and π electrons on aromatic rings. Judged by reaction constant k<inf>TST</inf> (1.17 × 10−20 s−1) in keto-enol tautomerism, phenolic –OH may not exist in keto form at 600 K. Consequently, subsequent chemical adsorption could not occur after physical adsorption of NH<inf>3</inf> onto phenolic –OH. Physical adsorption of NH<inf>3</inf> onto XLT could be verified by desorption of NH<inf>3</inf> in 200–300 °C analyzed by NH<inf>3</inf>-TPD. Hence, XLT and its derived semicoke mainly act as physical and chemical adsorption sites for NH<inf>3</inf>, respectively. This work could be beneficial to deep understanding of synergistic interactions in nitrogen fixation, as well as high-value-added utilization of nitrogen-rich biomass residue. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Silica-centered crosslinking solid polymer electrolyte for sodium metal batteries
Abstract: Replacing flammable liquid electrolytes with solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) can dramatically improve battery safety. Here, we report the development of silica (SiO<inf>2</inf>)-centered crosslinking SPEs by chemically bonding SiO<inf>2</inf> nanoparticles with the polymer matrix. This innovative design not only ensures the uniform dispersion of SiO<inf>2</inf> nanoparticles throughout the polymer matrix but also builds a robust interface between the nanofillers and the polymer matrix, thereby enhancing Na+ ionic conductivity. Simultaneously, it leverages the abundant hydroxyl (OH) groups on SiO<inf>2</inf> nanoparticles to interact with ClO<inf>4</inf>− anions through Lewis acid-base interactions and hydrogen bonding, promoting sodium salt dissociation. Theoretical calculations corroborate these interfacial mechanisms, revealing a 5.6-fold improvement in the Na+ diffusion coefficient. As a result, this pioneering design allows SPE to achieve a high Na+ ionic conductivity of 7.03 × 10−4 S cm−1 and an extended electrochemical voltage window up to 5.21 V. The assembled solid-state sodium metal batteries (with Na<inf>3</inf>V<inf>2</inf>(PO<inf>4</inf>)<inf>3</inf> as the cathode) exhibit dendrite-free Na-metal deposition, promising rate capability, and stable cycling performance with 84.6 % capacity retention over 200 cycles at 0.2C and 64.1 % capacity retention over 200 cycles at 1C. This work introduces a transformative strategy of engineering nanofiller–polymer interactions to enhance the properties of SPEs for solid-state batteries. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Integrated sewage sludge treatment for the sustainable recovery of fine-chemicals: Technical and economic analysis
Abstract: A sustainable procedure for effectively isolating grease from urban thickened sewage sludge was developed and examined. Thickened sludge underwent centrifugation, was treated with HCl and H<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf>, heated to 353 K and then centrifuged again. Besides a pure lipid current with a FFA content of 90–92 % (with a grease yield of up to 73.3 %), an aqueous acidic current and a wet residual solid cake (TS: 31.7 ± 3.4 %) were also generated. The technical integration of this procedure in conventional sludge-treatment lines were then investigated under pilot scale. The cogenerated streams were found to be digestible under anaerobic conditions, leading to a production of biomethane higher than that foreseeable based on the biomethanogenic potential of the starting sludge. This improvement of biomethane production demonstrated that the reactive step of the grease recovery process has a favorable effect on the digestibility of the residual sludge. Concomitantly, a reduction in the volumes of final sludge to be disposed of by 20 % was also determined. Alternatively, a different scenario of integration of the grease recovery was studied for WWTP not equipped with anaerobic digesters. The residual solid cake obtained from the lipid recovery process can be efficiently dried through a low-temperature desiccator. The desiccated cake (TS: 86.0 ± 6.0 %) had a high calorific value (17 MJ/Kg) capable of producing the electric and thermal energy needed for running the lipid recovery process. For both cases, the proposed integrated sewage sludge treatments could produce economic benefits capable of making the costs of investments recoverable within three years. These results pose the proposed grease recovery as a sustainable approach for the treatment of municipal sewage sludge, while facilitating the recovery of valuable resources. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Impact of heat pre-treatment on microbial succession and antibiotic resistance gene spread in high-solid anaerobic digestion of pig manure
Abstract: Two semi-continuous high-concentration anaerobic digestion (AD) trials were conducted over 70 days, during which the organic loading rate (OLR) was gradually increased from 3.33 to 9.30 g volatile solids L−1 d−1, aiming to investigate the effects of heat pre-treatment (HPT) on microbial succession and the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during high-solid AD of pig manure (PM). The reactor treating heat-pretreated PM achieved a maximum specific biogas yield of 484.81 mL g−1 VS, which was 55.75 % higher than that of the untreated control. HPT promoted the proliferation of the bacterial phylum Patescibacteria and the hydrogenotrophic archaeal genus Methanobacterium, facilitating syntrophic methanogenesis. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis indicated that HPT upregulated genes associated with CO₂-reducing methanogenesis and the biosynthesis of cofactors such as coenzyme F420 and methanofuran. ARG profiling revealed that both AD and HPT effectively suppressed the spread of ARGs, primarily by reducing the relative abundance of key microbial hosts such as Firmicutes. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into optimizing AD performance and microbial community structure while mitigating the environmental risks associated with ARG dissemination in PM. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Integrating flexibility and lattice engineering in Al[sbnd]Br Co-doped self-supporting LiMn2O4 electrodes for efficient lithium extraction
Abstract: Global new energy vehicle adoption and energy storage advancements have elevated lithium's strategic role in clean energy technologies. The supply-demand imbalance urgently requires efficient brine/seawater extraction methods to enable sustainable infrastructure and decarbonization. In this study, a novel flexible self-supporting electrode comprising Al[sbnd]Br co-doped lithium manganese oxide nanosheets grown directly onto carbon cloth (Al-Br-LMO NS@CC) was designed and fabricated for electrochemical lithium extraction. The electrode performance was improved via a multi-scale design: flexibility enhances kinetic adaptability, the self-supporting structure builds three-dimensional ion pathways, and Al[sbnd]Br co-doping triggers lattice reconstruction. Theoretical calculations reveal that Al[sbnd]Br co-doping promotes the conversion of Mn3+ to Mn4+ within the LMO lattice and narrows the band gap, effectively suppressing the Jahn-Teller effect and enhancing charge transport capability. The constructed Al-Br-LMO NS@CC electrode demonstrates outstanding lithium extraction performance in simulated brine, achieving a lithium uptake capacity of 5.25 mmol g−1 with an energy consumption as low as 0.15 Wh mol−1. This work provides a novel and robust platform for the advancement of highly efficient lithium extraction technologies from aqueous sources. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
